tasks.taskObjective: When offered a known reinforcing item or activity, the student will take/ use the item or activity.
tasks.question: When you hold out and offer a known reinforcer, will the student take the reinforcer?
tasks.examples: M & M taken and eaten
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= takes within 3 seconds all the time, 1= either not all the time or takes more than 3 seconds to respond

tasks.taskName: Take a reinforcer from two choices of items
tasks.taskObjective: When offered one reinforcing item or activity and another non-reinforcing item or activity, the student will select the reinforcing item or activity.
tasks.question: When you hold out and offer a reinforcer and a non-reinforcing item, will the student take the reinforcer?
tasks.examples: M & M vs. shoe, will take M&M
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= takes within 3 seconds all the time, 1= either not all the time or takes more than 3 seconds to respond

tasks.taskName: Look at a non- reinforcing item
tasks.taskObjective: Student will look at and track changes in location of a non- reinforcing item presented by an instructor.
tasks.question: If you hold up a non- reinforcing item, will the student look at it and watch it as you move it to different locations in front of the student?
tasks.examples: When you hold up a shoe and ask the student to look at the shoe, student will look at it and watch it as you move it to a variety of positions in front of him (e.g., up/ down/left/right)
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= will track the movement of the item to 6 different positions in a 10 second period, 3= will track the movement of the item to 4 positions in 10 seconds, 2= finds it in any position (up/down/left/ right) within 3 seconds, 1= will look at item but requires an additional prompt to look or takes more than 3 seconds to respond

tasks.taskName: Take a common object when offered
tasks.taskObjective: When offered a common object, the student will take the item.
tasks.question: When you hold out and offer an item, will the student take the object?
tasks.examples: When you hold out a shoe, student will take it
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= takes within 3 seconds all the time, 1= either not all the time or takes more than 3 seconds to respond

tasks.taskName: Approaches when a response is required for reinforcement
tasks.taskObjective: When a specific tangible reinforcer is available and there is a clearly identified requirement for a known response to be performed, the student will approach the instructor and perform the required response (i.e., the student knows that there is a reinforcer available but that he will need to approach the instructor and do a simple task to get the reinforcer).
tasks.question: When one of the child's reinforcers is available but the child must engage in a known response to receive the reinforcer, does the student approach and perform the response being requested? Do reinforcers maintain their value when simple responses (beyond approach and taking) are required?
tasks.examples: Instructor has raisins that the student enjoys (and student is hungry), the student walks across the room and performs an imitative response to get a raisin from the instructor
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= will approach and sit a table and perform multiple responses to get reinforcers (each response is reinforced), 3= will approach and perform multiple responses (each response is reinforced), 2= will readily and repeatedly approach and perform a variety of known single responses, 1= will occasionally approach and perform at least one response for the reinforcer

tasks.taskObjective: The student will work for instructor controlled reinforcement.
tasks.question: Do edible and other tangible items maintain their reinforcing value when delivered several times following requested responses?
tasks.examples: When given three pieces of a puzzle, one at a time, the student will put the pieces into a puzzle frame to get a raisin (a reinforcer) for each response
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= engages in 5 acquisition responses for at least 5 presentations of a particular reinforcer, 3= 2 acquisition & 3 maintenance responses for 5 presentations , 2= 5 maintenance responses for 5 presentations, 1= 3 maintenance responses for 3 presentations

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to demonstrate and use skills learned with one instructor when working with other instructors.
tasks.question: Does the student demonstrate and use skills learned with one instructor when working with other instructors?
tasks.examples: Student learns to imitate clapping hands and touching his nose with one instructor and then will do those same responses for other instructors
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= works readily with 3 or more instructors and with novel instructors at about the same rate and quality of responding demonstrated with familiar instructors, 1= works readily with 3 or more instructors at about the same rate and quality of responding

tasks.taskObjective: When an instructor is attempting to engage the student in learning activities (at a table, while seated on the floor, or standing near materials for an activity), the student will wait calmly, remain generally oriented towards the instructor and materials, and will keep his hands away from the instructional materials until an instruction is presented.
tasks.question: When the student is participating in learning activities, will he sit calmly, wait for the instructor to ask him to do a task, and keep his hands off the materials until he is told what to do?
tasks.examples: Sit calmly with hands on the table in front of, but not touching the materials, waiting to be asked to do a task, as opposed to requiring numerous prompts to "sit nicely," "keep hands back," etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= While sitting or standing in front of task materials the student consistently waits calmly orienting towards the materials without requiring prompts to leave the materials alone, 1= requires only one prompt to sit/stand nicely or keep hands off the materials

tasks.taskObjective: When engaged in an obvious series of learning tasks, the student will scan the materials and look at the instructor to seek the instruction for the next task.
tasks.question: When student is participating in a learning activity, does he scan the materials and then look at the instructor to see what he should do next?
tasks.examples: After scanning task pictures on the table, student looks at the instructor for the next instruction without having to be told to "Look."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= after scanning materials, student consistently looks to the instructor for the next instruction, 1= after scanning materials, student requires only one prompt to orient to the instructor for an instruction to be presented

tasks.taskName: Scans items in array before responding
tasks.taskObjective: When an instruction is presented during a series of learning tasks that involve instructional materials, the student will attend to the instruction then scan the materials prior to responding to the instruction.
tasks.question: When student is participating in a learning activity that involves instructional materials, does the student scan the materials prior to responding to instructions?
tasks.examples: When instructed to "give me shoe," the student will scan all the items in the immediate area until he locates the shoe.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can consistently scan up to 6 task-related items within 3 seconds (prior to responding), 1= can consistently scan up to 3 task-related items within 3 seconds (prior to responding)

tasks.taskName: Responds quickly when given an instruction
tasks.taskObjective: When engaged in a series of learning tasks, the student will respond quickly when an instruction is presented.
tasks.question: When student is given an instruction while participating in a learning activity, does he follow the instruction immediately after it is given?
tasks.examples: When asked to point to a picture of a bird, the student immediately begins to reach toward and then point to the bird.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= consistently responds within 3 seconds when instructions are presented, 1= consistently responds within 5 seconds when instructions are presented

tasks.taskObjective: A variety of items and activities serve as reinforcers
tasks.question: Will the student work for a variety of items and activities as reinforcement?
tasks.examples: Actions: tickle, pick-up, visual- toy that spins, Auditory: music, Tactile: rubs & tickles, Social: claps, praise, Toys: specific ones, Activities: puzzles, computer
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= at least 10 separate instructor controllable items or activities are effective as reinforcers for learning behaviors, 1=at least 5 items or activities are effective as reinforcers

tasks.taskObjective: The student will work for intermittent reinforcement.
tasks.question: Will the student work for intermittent (occasionally delivered) reinforcement?
tasks.examples: Student will label picture cards when he is occasionally given a raisin after (a reinforcer) an average of about 4 responses
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= engages in 5 acquisition responses for an edible or tangible reinforcer, 3=2 acquisition & 3 maintenance responses for a reinforcer 2=4 maintenance responses for an edible or tangible reinforcer 1=2 maintenance responses for an edible or tangible reinforcer

tasks.taskObjective: The student will work for reinforcement that involves fun interaction with the instructor.
tasks.question: Will the student work to get to do a fun activity (reinforcement) with the instructor?
tasks.examples: The student performs tasks to get to play "Ring Around the Rosie" with the instructor
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= engages in 5 acquisition responses for instructor interaction reinforcer, 3=2 acquisition & 3 maintenance responses for instructor interaction 2= 4 maintenance responses for instructor interaction, 1=2 maintenance responses for instructor interaction reinforcer

tasks.taskName: Looks for instructor's change in facial expression and voice
tasks.taskObjective: After completing a task, when engaged in a series of learning activities, the student will orient to the instructor such as to observe the changes in instructor's facial expression and voice that provide feedback regarding the correctness of the response.
tasks.question: When student is participating in a learning activity, does he look for changes in instructor's facial expression and voice that provide feedback regarding the correctness of the response?
tasks.examples: Looks to see if the instructor is smiling, listens to the change in inflection in the instructor's voice as praise is being delivered
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= looks at instructors to seek feedback when finished responding at least 70% of the time, 1= occasionally looks at instructors to seek feedback when finished responding (without the instructor using highly exaggerated changes in behavior to get the student to notice)

tasks.taskObjective: Praise will serve as an effective reinforcer for the student.
tasks.question: Does praise serve as an effective reinforcer?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= works for 15 minutes for only praise, 3= works for praise for 15 min. with a back-up reinforcer, 2= works for praise for 5 min. with back-up reinforcer, 1= works for praise for 3 responses prior to receiving a back-up reinforcer

tasks.taskName: Waits appropriately if reinforcer delivery is delayed
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to wait appropriately if a reinforcer is not delivered immediately following a behavior.
tasks.question: Does the student wait appropriately if a reinforcer is not delivered immediately following a behavior?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= waits 5 minutes, 3=1 minute, 2=10 seconds, 1=5 seconds

tasks.taskObjective: The student will seek recognition for his accomplishments.
tasks.question: Does the student seek approval for work which he has done well or completed?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= asks others to see what they have done, 1= looks to see if others have noticed what they have done

tasks.taskObjective: Completion of a task serves as an effective reinforcer for the student.
tasks.question: Does the completion of a task serve as an effective reinforcer?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= works independently 10 minutes to complete task for recognition of task completion, 1= works independently for 5 minutes to complete a task with only praise as the reinforcer

tasks.taskName: Puzzle with a single-piece type of inset
tasks.taskObjective: When given single, uniquely- shaped pieces from an inset puzzle; the student will put the puzzle pieces into the puzzle frame.
tasks.question: Can the student put single, uniquely-shaped puzzle pieces into a frame board?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= places 5 pieces presented as group by looking and positioning, 3= 3 pieces presented as group by looking and positioning 2= 5 pieces handed separately using trial and error 1= places up to 3 pieces handed separately using trial and error

tasks.taskObjective: When provided a form box or shape sorter and its pieces, the student will be able to put the pieces into the corresponding holes in the form box.
tasks.question: Can the student put pieces in a form box or shape sorter?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 6 pieces by looking at piece then visually locating the corresponding hole, 3= 4 pieces by look and locate, 2= 4 pieces using trial and error approach, 1= 2 pieces by trial and error

tasks.taskObjective: When given an object the student will match to an identical object in an array of three items.
tasks.question: Can the student match objects to an identical object presented in an array of three items?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 objects to objects in a display of 8 items, 3= at least 5 objects to objects in a display of 4 items, 2= at least two objects to objects in a display of 2 items, 1= can match one object to an identical object in a display of 2 items

tasks.taskObjective: When given an item, the student will match the object to one of three pictures in an array.
tasks.question: Can the student match objects to corresponding pictures?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can match three items in succession, 1= can match a single item per task presentation

tasks.taskObjective: When given a picture, the student will match to an identical picture in an array of three pictures.
tasks.question: Can the student match pictures to an identical picture presented in an array of three pictures?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 pictures to pictures in a display of 8 pictures, 3= at least 5 pictures to pictures in display of 4, 2= at least two pictures to pictures in a display of 2, 1= can match one picture to an identical picture in a display of 2 pictures

tasks.taskObjective: When given a picture of an item, the student will match the picture to one of three objects in an array.
tasks.question: Can the student match pictures of objects to corresponding objects?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can match three items in succession, 1= can match a single item per task presentation

tasks.taskObjective: When given a group of ten pictures of items, the student will match those pictures to an identical picture in an array of ten pictures in quick succession.
tasks.question: Is the student able to match pictures to an identical picture in an array of ten pictures in a one-after-the-other manner?
tasks.examples: When given a stack of pictures, student matches each one to another in an array of pictures in rapid succession
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can match at least 10 items in 30 seconds, 1= can match 5 separate items in 15 seconds

tasks.taskObjective: When given a variety of non- identical objects or pictures representing three items, and given an array of sample items for each of the three items, the student will sort non identical items into the appropriate groups (e.g., all the dogs, all the trees, all the people).
tasks.question: Can the student sort non- identical items into piles when samples of those items are displayed in an array (e.g., dogs, trees, people)?
tasks.examples: Student is given a mixed set of various pictures of dogs and trees and a sample of each is placed on the table. The student sorts pictures by placing dogs on the pile of dogs and the trees on the pile of trees.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= given 20 items (5 each of 4 items), can sort 10 or more types of items into an array of 4 samples, 3= given 12 items (3 each of 4 items), can sort at least 6 types of items into array of 4 samples, 2= given 6 items (2 each of 3 items), can sort at least 4 types of items into array of 3 samples, 1=given 4 items (2 each of 2 items), can sort 2 types of items into an array of 2 samples
tasks.protocolNotes: Modified. Note: This skill does not require the student to receptively know the class of the items. It requires only visual matching of similar, non-identical items.

tasks.taskObjective: When given a block design card, student will place the blocks in the appropriate location on the design card disregarding extra blocks.
tasks.question: Can the student do block designs on a picture card?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can quickly complete designs with 6 or more blocks (some extras), 3= 4 or more blocks (some extras), 2= can do up to 4 blocks (no extras), 1= can do designs using 2 blocks (no extras)

tasks.taskName: Puzzles with multiple connecting pieces in an inset-type frame
tasks.taskObjective: When given uniquely-shaped, connecting puzzle pieces which fit into an irregularly shaped inset frame, the student will complete the puzzle.
tasks.question: Can the student complete puzzles with uniquely-shaped connecting pieces which fit into an irregularly- shaped inset frame?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 4 puzzles with 8 pieces, 3=4 puzzles with 5 pieces, 2=2 puzzles with 5 pieces, 1= 1 puzzle with at least 5 pieces

tasks.taskName: Puzzles with a square-edged border frame
tasks.taskObjective: When given a square-edged framed puzzle, the student will complete the puzzle.
tasks.question: Can the student complete puzzles with connecting pieces which fit into a square-edged frame?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 3 puzzles with 5 pieces, 3=3 puzzles with 4 pieces, 2=3 puzzles with 3 pieces, 1=3 puzzles with at least 2 pieces
tasks.protocolNotes: Note: The pieces may either connect to each other (like a jig saw puzzle), or they may slide next to each other without connecting.

tasks.taskObjective: When given a block design card, student will place blocks to make the design shown on the card.
tasks.question: Can the student do block designs from looking at a picture of a design?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can quickly complete designs with 6 or more pieces (some extra blocks), 3= 4 or more parts (extras), 2= can do up to 4 pieces (no extras), 1= can do designs using 2 blocks (no extra blocks)

tasks.taskName: Sequence pattern to match a visual model
tasks.taskObjective: When given a visual sequence pattern consisting of items (e.g., colored blocks), the student will arrange items to match the pattern.
tasks.question: Can the student match a pattern of visual stimuli?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can match sequence of 8 pieces comprised of 4 different items when given extra pieces, 3= 8 pieces of 4 items with no extras, 2= 6 pieces of three items with no extras, 1= 6 pieces of two items with no extras

tasks.taskName: Puzzles with multiple pieces which must be juxtaposed
tasks.taskObjective: When given irregularly- shaped, non-interlocking puzzle pieces, student will correctly juxtapose the pieces to form a picture.
tasks.question: When there is no frame, can the student juxtapose (i.e., place together) non-interlocking puzzle pieces to make a picture?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 4 puzzles with 5 pieces, 3=4 puzzles with 4 pieces, 2=2 puzzles with 3 pieces, 1= 1 puzzle with at least 3 pieces

tasks.taskObjective: When given a standard jigsaw puzzle (interlocking pieces without a frame), the student will correctly complete the puzzle.
tasks.question: Can the student complete standard jigsaw puzzles (i.e., interlocking pieces without a frame)?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least four puzzles with 12 pieces, 3= two puzzles with 12 pieces, 2= two puzzles with 8 pieces, 1= one puzzle with at least 8 pieces

tasks.taskObjective: Given an array of items or pictures, the student will be able to match an item that is associated with one of the items in the array (e.g., match a bat to picture of a ball).
tasks.question: When given a display of objects or pictures and given a different item, can the student match the item from the display that is associated with the item being presented (e.g., match a bat to a ball when shown an array of a ball, a cup, and a shoe)?
tasks.examples: bat and a ball; cup and juice; socks and shoes; knife, fork, spoon and plate; shirt, hat and pants
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can match at least 2 related pictures for 20 or more items, 3= 2 related pictures for 10 items, 2= 1 related picture for 10 items, 1= can match at least 1 related picture for 5 items

tasks.taskObjective: When provided with a sample of two items that have different functions and shown a demonstration of matching another item that has the same function, the student will be able to sort additional pictures that have the same functions with the correct sample items.
tasks.question: When provided with a model of items that are used for a certain function, can the student sort pictures of items into groups of items that have the same function (e.g., scissors with ones you cut with, pen with things you write with)?
tasks.examples: When shown a pen and a bottle of bubbles and the placement of a crayon on the pen and a candle on the bubbles, student continues to place other pictures on things you write with and things you blow on the correct piles.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 5 items from 4 functions , 3= at least 5 items from 3 functions, 2= at least 5 items from 2 functions, 1= at least 2 items from 2 functions

tasks.taskObjective: When provided with a sample of two of items that have different features/parts and shown a demonstration of matching another item that has the same feature/part, the student will be able to sort additional pictures that have the same features/parts with the correct sample items.
tasks.question: When provided with a model of items that have a certain feature/part, can the student sort pictures of items into groups of items that have the same feature/part (e.g., dog with the ones that have tails, car with the ones that have wheels, blue items with blue items, striped items with other things that have stripes)?
tasks.examples: When shown a monkey and a car and the placement of a dog on the monkey and a bicycle on the car, student continues to place other pictures on things with tails and things with wheels.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 5 items from 4 features/parts, 3= at least 5 items from 3 features/parts, 2= at least 5 items from 2 features/parts, 1= at least 2 items from 2 features/parts

tasks.taskObjective: When provided with a sample of three different classes of items and shown a demonstration of matching another member of each class, the student will be able to sort additional pictures that match the class to which the item belongs.
tasks.question: Can the student sort pictures of items into classes to which the item belongs when provided with a model of items from each class (e.g., dog with other animals, shirt with other clothing)?
tasks.examples: When shown a cat and a shoe and the placement of a dog on the cat and a shirt on the shoe, student continues to place other pictures of animals and clothing on the correct piles.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 5 items from 4 classes, 3= at least 5 items from 3 classes, 2= at least 5 items from 2 classes, 1= at least 2 items from 2 classes

tasks.taskObjective: After having been shown a model of items in a specific sequence and then having the model removed, the student will be able to replicate the sequence.
tasks.question: Can the student replicate a sequence of items after having been shown a model of items in a specific sequence and then having the model removed?
tasks.examples: After showing a pattern of three items and then remove the display, the student replicates the pattern.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= immediately, with three items after 5 second delay,3= three items with two second delay or two items with 5 second delay, 2= two items in two seconds without prompts, 1= two items with 2 second delay with only verbal or gestural prompts

tasks.taskObjective: When shown a specific item and it is removed, and five items are then presented (one being the same as the original item), the student will be able to find the initial item.
tasks.question: Can the student find an item which had previously been shown to the student after it has been removed, and then presented in an array of three items (one being the same as the original item)?
tasks.examples: After showing the student a picture of a cat, hide the picture, wait a few seconds, present pictures of a dog, cat, and bird and say "Find the same" or "Find it"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= after 5 second delay, can find any one of 10 items within 3 seconds, when presented an array of 5 items, 3= after 3 second delay, can find any one of 5 items within 3 seconds, 2= after 3 second delay, can find any one of 5 items within 3 seconds, when presented an array of 3 items, 1= after 2 second delay, can find any one of 3 items within 3 seconds, when presented an array of 2 items

tasks.taskObjective: When given a model of items in a specific sequence (regular and irregular), the student will be able to continue adding items in the correct sequence (e.g., ABABAB, ABCABC, ABBABB, AABAAB, ABBCABBC).
tasks.question: Can the student continue adding items in the correct sequence when given a model of items in a specific sequence?
tasks.examples: When an arrangement of blocks are displayed in a pattern (e.g., a red block, blue block, red block, blue block, etc.) the student continues to add a red block, then a blue block, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= continues an irregular pattern with at least 3 different stimuli with irrelevant pieces present, 3= three items in a regular sequence with extra irrelevant pieces present, 2= three items in a regular sequence, 1= two items in an alternating sequence

tasks.taskObjective: Given a set of blocks or other items and a model of a simple 3-dimensional object (e.g., a house, car), the student will be able to arrange the blocks or other items to replicate the structure.
tasks.question: When given a simple 3- dimensional model, can the student arrange blocks and other items to make a duplicate structure (e.g., a house, car)?
tasks.examples: When shown a model, the student builds a simple house using blocks.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can replicate 2 objects using at least 6 blocks or other items, 1= can replicate 2 objects using at least 3 blocks or other items

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to observe a person placing multiple identical objects on a table and then place a different item on each of those items immediately after each one of the first type of item has been placed.
tasks.question: If a person put a set of identical items on a table, is the student able to place a second item on each of those placed items immediately after each of the first items was placed on the table?
tasks.examples: For each napkin placed on a table, the student immediately places a spoon on the napkin; after each instructor- placed white block the student adds a blue block; for every juice container put on a table, the student immediately puts a straw next to each container
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can immediately place an item on a corresponding item for a series of at least 6 responses, 1= can immediately place an item on a corresponding item for a series of at least 3 responses

tasks.taskObjective: When given a model of the start and end of a continuum, student will be able to arrange additional task stimuli in the appropriate order by size, quantity, shade of color, and sequence.
tasks.question: Can the student arrange items in a logical order (i.e., by size, quantity, shade of color, sequence of completion, order -- ABC's, 123's)?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can arrange at least four sets of items for each of the four specified attributes, 3= two sets of items for three attributes, 2= two sets of items for two attributes, 1= two sets of items for one attribute

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to arrange a set of picture cards in the appropriate sequence.
tasks.question: Can the student arrange pictures depicting a logical sequence of events?
tasks.examples: Places four pictures of washing hand sequence in order: Turn on water, use soap, rinse hands, dry hands with towel
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can arrange at least five sets of four items in a sequence, 3= five sets of items with a three-card sequence, 2= three sets of items with a three-card sequence, 1= two sets of items with a three-card sequence

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to draw a line from the start to the end of simple mazes.
tasks.question: Can the student draw a line from the start to the end of simple mazes?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can draw a line from start to end in a maze which has 3 choice points for selecting the correct path, 1= can draw a line in a maze which has only 1 choice point for selecting the correct path

tasks.taskObjective: Student will look at or come to a person when called by his name.
tasks.question: Will the student look at or come to a person when called by his name?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= looks or comes at least 80% of the time, 1= requires some prompts to respond

tasks.taskName: Follow instructions to do an enjoyable action in context
tasks.taskObjective: When given instructions to do a preferred activity in the context of the ongoing activity, the student will comply with the instructions.
tasks.question: Will the student follow an instruction to do an enjoyable action under the conditions when the activity usually occurs (e.g., "Go swing" at recess)?
tasks.examples: Jump on trampoline, swing, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 3 activities without prompts, 3= at least 3 activities with only one additional verbal or pointing prompt, 2= 3 or more activities with a model and no physical prompts, 1= 3 or more activities with only partial physical prompts

tasks.taskName: Follow instructions to look at a reinforcing item
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will look at a reinforcing item held by an instructor.
tasks.question: If you hold up a reinforcing item and ask the student to look at it, will the student look at the item?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= looks at it in any position (up/down/left/ right) within 3 seconds, 1= will look at item but requires an additional prompt to look or takes more than 3 seconds to respond

tasks.taskName: Follow instructions to touch a reinforcing item in various positions
tasks.taskObjective: Upon instruction, the student will touch a preferred item held in various positions.
tasks.question: If you hold up a desirable item in various locations, will he reach out and touch or grab it on instruction (e.g., "Touch___," or "(name of item)"?
tasks.examples: Potato chip held over head, off to side, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily touches an item in any position (up/down/ left/ right) within 3 seconds, 1= touches or grabs an item within 3 seconds if it is held in front of him

tasks.taskName: Follow instructions to touch a common item in various positions
tasks.taskObjective: Upon instruction, the student will touch a common item held in various positions.
tasks.question: If you hold up a common item in various locations, will he reach out and touch it on instruction (e.g., "Touch___," or "(name of item)"?
tasks.examples: Pen held over head, off to side, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily touches an item in any position (up/down/ left/ right) within 3 seconds, 1= touches or grabs an item within 3 seconds if it is held in front of him

tasks.taskName: Follow instructions to do an enjoyable action out of context
tasks.taskObjective: The student will comply with instructions to do a preferred activity even though it is not occurring at that time.
tasks.question: Will the student follow an instruction to do an enjoyable action even when it is not under the conditions which the activity usually occurs (e.g., "Go swing" while inside)?
tasks.examples: While sitting at a table, the child will follow an instruction to "go jump on trampoline," etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 3 activities without prompts, 3= at least 3 with only one verbal or pointing prompt, 2= 3 or more with a model and no physical prompts, 1=3 or more activities with only partial physical prompts
tasks.protocolNotes: Modified. Note: Following an instruction with a prompt is not a true compliance with the instructor's verbal behavior but does begin to establish instructional control that is critical to the development of actual "receptive" skills

tasks.taskObjective: The student will comply with the instructions to do a non- preferred activity when the activity is presently occurring.
tasks.question: Will the student follow an instruction to do a non- preferred activity at the time when the activity usually occurs (e.g., "Wash hands" before lunch)?
tasks.examples: After using the toilet, the student will follow directions to "wash hands."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 3 activities without prompts, 3= at least 3 with only one verbal or pointing prompt, 2= 3 or more with a model and no physical prompts, 1=3 or more activities with only partial physical prompts

tasks.taskName: Follow instructions to give a named, non-reinforcing object
tasks.taskObjective: The student will follow instructions which require him to give a named, non- reinforcing item.
tasks.question: When an adult holds out his hand and asks for an item, will the student follow instructions to give a named, non-desired item?
tasks.examples: Upon request the child will hand a shoe to an instructor.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= usually within 3 seconds, 1= usually with one additional prompt (not including holding out hand to receive the item)
tasks.protocolNotes: Modified. Note: This task does not require the student to be able to receptively know the name of the item to select it from a group of items

tasks.taskName: Follow instructions to do a simple motor action
tasks.taskObjective: The student will comply with instructions to do a simple motor task (e.g., clap, turn around, arms up).
tasks.question: Will the student follow an instruction to do a simple motor action upon request (e.g., "Clap hands")?
tasks.examples: Jump, sit down, arms up, clap, blow, knock.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 6 instructions without prompts and can follow at least 4 different actions within 10 seconds 3= at least 6 instructions without prompts 2= at least 4 instructions without prompts, 1= at least 2 instructions without prompts
tasks.protocolNotes: Modified. See Appendix 2: Simple Instruction List

tasks.taskName: Follow instructions to touch item vs. a distracter
tasks.taskObjective: When asked to touch an object that is being held and an empty hand is held out as a distracter (or the object is placed on a table with another neutral item such a styrofoam cube used as a distracter), the student will touch the named object.
tasks.question: If you hold up an object in one hand and hold up your other empty hand (or the object is placed on a table with another neutral item such a styrofoam cube used as a distracter) will the student touch the named object when instructed?
tasks.examples: When a cup is held on one side, and an empty hand is held in a different position, the student will select "cup" upon request.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily finds and touches it in any position within 3 seconds, 1= touches an item if it is held in front of him
tasks.protocolNotes: Modified. NOTE: The receptive discrimination skills for tasks C 10 - C 17 can be demonstrated with any type of selection response (e.g., point to, pick up, give me, touch, show me, where is, find the ___)

tasks.taskName: Follow instructions to select one reinforcing item from an array of two objects
tasks.taskObjective: When asked, the student will select a named reinforcing item from an array of two objects held or placed in any position in front of him.
tasks.question: If you hold up or place two items in any position near the student (one being a reinforcer) and ask him to select the reinforcer, can he do it?
tasks.examples: When a shoe is held on one side, and a bottle of bubbles (a reinforcer) is held in a different position, the student will select "bubbles" upon request.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily finds and selects it in any position within 3 seconds, 1= finds and selects item if it is held in front of him
tasks.protocolNotes: Modified. See Appendix 3: Receptive and Label List

tasks.taskName: Follow instructions to select one of two reinforcing items
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, the student will be able to select an object named by the instructor from an array of two reinforcing objects held or placed in any position in front of him.
tasks.question: If you hold up or place two reinforcing objects in any position near the student and ask him to select one of them, can he do it?
tasks.examples: When a box of raisins (reinforcer) and a bottle of bubbles (a reinforcer) are held in front of the student, the student will select "bubbles" upon request.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily finds and selects it in any position within 3 seconds, 1= finds and selects item if it is held in front of him
tasks.protocolNotes: Modified. See Appendix 3: Receptive and Label List

tasks.taskName: Follow instructions to select one of two common objects
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, the student will be able to select an object named by the instructor from an array of two common objects held or placed in any position in front of him.
tasks.question: Can the student select a specified object from a selection of two common objects?
tasks.examples: When a cup and a shoe are held in front of the student, the student will select "shoe" upon request.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= receptively identifies 50 or more objects and can identify several different examples of most of those objects, 3= identifies at least one example of 25 objects, 2=10 objects, 1= identifies at least 2 objects
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendix 3: Receptive and Label List Note that objects selected should be ones that the student hears the names of and interacts with on a frequent basis.

tasks.taskName: Select one of two pictures of common items
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will select a picture named by the instructor from an array of two pictures of common items held or placed in any position in front of him.
tasks.question: Can the student select a specified picture of an item from a selection of two pictures of common items?
tasks.examples: When a picture of a dog and a picture of a shoe are held in front of the student, the student will select "shoe" upon request.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= receptively identifies pictures of 50 or more items and can identify several different pictures of most of those items, 3=25 pictures of different items, 2=10 pictures, 1=2 pictures
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendix 3: Receptive and Label List

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to follow directions to touch parts of his own body.
tasks.question: If you ask the student to touch a part of his body, can he do it?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=10 or more parts, 3= 6 parts, 2= 4 parts, 1 = 2 parts

tasks.taskName: Select one of six or more objects on a table
tasks.taskObjective: The student will select a specified object for at least 100 common objects when the object is presented in an array of six or more objects on a table in any position in front of the student.
tasks.question: If you place six or more objects on a table in any position and ask the student to select one of those items, can he select the named object?
tasks.examples: This skill can be demonstrated with any type of selection response (e.g., point to, pick up, give me, touch, show me, where is, find the)
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= receptively identifies 100 or more objects and can identify several different examples (including novel examples) of most of those objects when presented in an array of six or more objects, 3= 50 objects of at least one example of the item when presented in an array of three objects, 2= 10 objects (array of 3), 1=5 objects when presented in an array of three objects
tasks.protocolNotes: Modified. See Appendix 3: Receptive and Label List

tasks.taskName: Select one of six or more pictures on a table
tasks.taskObjective: The student will select a specified picture for at least 100 common objects when the picture is presented in an array of six or more pictures on a table in any position in front of the student.
tasks.question: If you place six or more pictures of common objects on a table in any position and ask the student to select one of those items, can he select the named object?
tasks.examples: This skill can be demonstrated with any type of selection response (e.g., point to, pick up, give me, touch, show me, where is, find the)
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= receptively identifies 100 or more pictures and can identify several different examples (including novel examples) of most of those pictures when presented in an array of six or more pictures, 3= 50 pictures of at least one example of the item when presented in an array of three or more pictures, 2=10 pictures (array of 3), 1=5 pictures when presented in an array of three or more pictures
tasks.protocolNotes: Modified. See Appendix 3: Receptive and Label List

tasks.taskName: Acquires new selection skills without intensive training
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to acquire selection skills for many new common objects or pictures of items after being required to select the items less than five times.
tasks.question: Does the student learn new receptive discrimination skills for new common items within five presentations?
tasks.examples: Student learns to select a picture of a "telephone" in five or less training trials.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily learns to select many new items after being required to select the items less than 5 times, 1= selects many new items after being required to select the items less than 10 times.

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to point to or select known items from an array upon request when presented in quick succession.
tasks.question: Is the student able to point to or select known items from an array upon request when presented in a one-after-the-other manner?
tasks.examples: When asked to "point to shoe", child does, and then points to a "cup," "book," and "apple" in rapid succession
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can sequentially point to or select at least 10 known items in 30 seconds, 1= can point to or select 5 separate known items in 15 seconds

tasks.taskName: Varied instructions to select using any response
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to select objects and pictures named by the instructor while using a variety of instructions to select those items (e.g. "Show me ___," "Where is the ___," "Can you find the ___," "Touch the ___").
tasks.question: Can the student select specified objects and pictures when provided with a variety of instructions to select those items (e.g. "Show me ___," "Where is the ___," "Can you find the ___," "Touch the ___")?
tasks.examples: "Show me ___," "Where is the ___," "Can you find the ___," "Touch the ___," "Do you see a ___," "Find the ___."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= selects objects and pictures when given any of 5 instructions to select a specified item (any selection response is acceptable), 1= selects objects and pictures when given any 2 instructions to select a specified item (can use any response)

tasks.taskName: Point to body parts on others or pictures
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to follow directions to point to body parts of other people or touch pictures of body parts.
tasks.question: If you ask the student to point to body parts of other people or touch pictures of body parts, can he do it?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=10 or more parts, 3= 6 parts, 2= 4 parts, 1 = 2 parts

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to follow directions to touch clothing items on his own body.
tasks.question: If you ask the student to touch a piece of clothing on his body, can he do it?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= 4 or more items, 1=2 items

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to follow directions to touch specified parts of items (e.g., door and window of a house, wheel and door of a car)
tasks.question: If you ask the student to show you the parts of an item (picture or object), can he point to the named parts?
tasks.examples: When looking at a picture of a house, the student can point to the door, window and roof.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 3 or more parts of ten objects, 3= 3 parts of six objects, 2=2 parts of four objects, 1 = at least 2 parts of two objects

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to select between two similar items that vary on one dimension (i.e., adjectives).
tasks.question: Can the student select a specific item when you hold up two items that vary in only one dimension (i.e., adjectives)?
tasks.examples: red block vs. blue block ... big/ little, hot/cold, old/new, fat/thin, wet/dry, fast/slow, day/night, hard/soft, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= selects at least 20 adjectives (including at least 3 colors, 2 shapes and 2 sizes), 3= at least 10 adjectives (at least 5 of which are not colors), 2= at least 5 adjectives (may be all colors), 1= can identify at least one adjective
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendices 5 & 6: Adjectives List & Colors and Shapes List

tasks.taskName: Selects items by following another's gaze
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to select an item by attending to the eye orientation of another person.
tasks.question: If you ask the student to "Give me that one," while looking at a specific item, will the student be able to select the correct item?
tasks.examples: When a pen, a crayon, and a piece of chalk are on different parts of a table, the student selects the item to which the instructor is looking.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can select one of three separated items located on a table, 1= can select one of two separated items located on a table

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to follow hand signals from an adult to come, sit, stand, go to a location, and perform an action when signaled (e.g., stand up or clap hands when point to the child).
tasks.question: Does the student follow hand signals from an adult to come to the adult, sit down, stand, and go to a location to which the adult is pointing, and perform an action when signaled?
tasks.examples: Student goes to door when adult points to the door, student claps his hands when the adult points to him (to indicate his turn), student selects the big cup when teacher points to the largest of several cups on a table.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can respond correctly to all 5 types of hand signals, 3= can respond correctly to at least 4 types of hand signals, 2= can respond correctly to at least 3 types of hand signals, 1=can respond to at least 2 types of hand signals

tasks.taskName: Follow an instruction to go to a person
tasks.taskObjective: Student will be able to walk across the room to go to a specified person.
tasks.question: Can the student walk across the room to go to a specified person?
tasks.examples: Student follows an instruction by walking across the room when told to "go to Jim"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can go to at least four people upon request, 1= can go to at least two people upon request

tasks.taskName: Follow an instruction to give an item to a person or place item on an object
tasks.taskObjective: Student will be able to walk across the room to go to a specified place or person and place or deliver an item (e.g., give pen to Jim).
tasks.question: Can the student walk across the room to go to a specified place or person and place or deliver an item?
tasks.examples: "Give the pen to Jim"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can go to at least 2 people and 2 places and deliver/place a given item, 3= 2 people or places without prompts, 2= 2 people or places with only a single verbal prompt, 1=1 person or place with only a verbal prompt

tasks.taskName: Follow an instruction to walk to someone and get a named item
tasks.taskObjective: Student will be able to walk across the room to go to a specified place or person and get a requested item.
tasks.question: Can you ask the student walk across the room to go to a specified place or person and get a requested item?
tasks.examples: "Go get the book from the desk and bring it to me"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can go to at least 2 people and 2 places and get a specified item, 3= 2 people or places without prompts, 2= 2 people or places with only a single verbal prompt, 1=1 person or place with only a verbal prompt

tasks.taskName: Follow an instruction to go to a person and do an action
tasks.taskObjective: Student will be able to walk across the room to go to a specified person and perform a stated action (e.g., give Jim a hug).
tasks.question: Can you ask the student to go to a person and perform an action (e.g., give a hug)?
tasks.examples: "Give Jim a hug"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can go to at least three people and perform at least 2 actions, 3= 2 people & 2 actions, 2= 2 people & 1 action, 1=1 person & 1 action

tasks.taskName: Specific motor responses in receptive tasks
tasks.taskObjective: The student will select common objects and pictures with a specific motor response when given a variety of instructions specifying the response required to select those items (e.g., "Touch," "Point to," "Give me," "Pick up," "Get the").
tasks.question: Can the student make selections of objects and pictures when given a variety of instructions which specify the response required to select those items (e.g., "Touch," "Point to," "Give me," "Pick up," "Get" )?
tasks.examples: "Touch the cup," "Point to bird," "Give me shoe," "Pick up hat," "Get the plate," "Cover the monkey," "Hide the spoon," "Push the car"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= responds correctly to any of 5 different selection responses, 3= four different selection responses, 2= three different selection responses, 1= two different selection responses
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendix 7: Receptive Instruction List When given a specific instruction that specifies the response required to select those items (e.g., "Touch," "Point to," "Give me," "Pick up," "Get the") the student will use the specified response

tasks.taskName: Demonstrates a specified action with an object when given different objects
tasks.taskObjective: The student will comply with instructions to do a simple action when presented with several objects, one of which is used to perform the action.
tasks.question: Will the student follow an instruction to do a simple action when presented with several objects, one of which is used to perform the action (e.g., display of a pencil and a pillow and instructed to "Show me writing")?
tasks.examples: "Show me... sleeping, writing, tapping, cutting, rolling."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= at least 5 without prompts, 1= at least 2 with only verbal or pointing prompts

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to perform a specified action with a specific object, when several different objects are present that could be used to demonstrate the requested action.
tasks.question: Can the student demonstrate actions using a variety of objects (e.g., with a car, a train, a ball, a brush, and a toy dog present, student can follow directions to show me "brushing dog," "brushing arm," "rolling car," "rolling ball," etc.)?
tasks.examples: "Bounce ball, roll ball, throw ball," "Brush hair, brush dog."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can perform at least 4 actions on at least 4 objects, 3= can perform at least 3 actions on 4 objects, 2= can perform at least 2 actions on 4 objects, 1= can perform 2 actions on at least 2 objects

tasks.taskObjective: The student will comply with instructions to do a pretend activity.
tasks.question: Will the student follow an instruction to do an action even when it is not the conditions under which the activity usually occurs (e.g., "Show me laughing")?
tasks.examples: "Show me... laughing, crying, yawning, sleeping, writing, tapping, cutting, rolling."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= at least 5 without prompts, 1= at least 2 with only verbal or pointing prompts

tasks.taskName: Select one of three pictures representing actions
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, the student will select a specified action picture from an array of three pictures on a table in any position in front of the student.
tasks.question: Can the student select a specified picture of an action from a selection of three pictures representing actions?
tasks.examples: When shown pictures of a boy writing, kicking, and eating and asked to select the picture of "writing" the student selects the picture of the boy writing
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= selects 20 or more action pictures and can identify several different examples (including novel examples) of most of those actions, 3=10 actions, 2=5 actions, 1= 2 action pictures
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendix 8: Actions and Verbs List Note: This skill can be demonstrated with any type of selection response (e.g., point to, pick up, give me, touch, show me, where is, find the)

tasks.taskObjective: Given an array of items or pictures and asked, "What goes with this?," the student will be able to select the item which is used with the item being shown (e.g., select a bat when shown a picture of a ball).
tasks.question: When given a display of objects or pictures and shown a different item and asked, "What goes with this?," can the student select an item from the display which is used with the item being presented (e.g., select a bat when shown a picture of a ball)?
tasks.examples: bat and a ball; cup and juice; socks and shoes; knife, fork and a spoon; shirt, hat and pants
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can select at least 2 related pictures for 20 or more items, 3= 2 related pictures for 10 items, 2= 1 related picture for 10 items, 1= can select at least 1 related picture for 5 items

tasks.taskObjective: Student will be able to select objects or pictures of items when told the item's function.
tasks.question: Can the student select objects or pictures of items when told the item's function [e.g., Give me the one(s) you cut with, write with, etc.]?
tasks.examples: When shown pictures of a scissors, a shoe and a horse, and asked "Which one do you cut with?;" the student will select scissors.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can select at least 25 items when told the item's function and can select 2 or more items with a specified function from a display of at least 6 items, 3= at least 25 items, 2= at least 5, 1= at least 2 items

tasks.taskObjective: Student will be able to select objects or pictures of items when told the item's features or parts.
tasks.question: Can the student select objects or pictures of items when told the item's features or parts [e.g., Give me the one(s) with a tail]?
tasks.examples: When shown pictures of a scissors, a shoe and a horse, and asked "Which one has a tail?;" the student will select the horse.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can select at least 2 features or parts for 25 items and can select 2 or more items with a specified feature/part from a display of at least 6 items, 3= at least 2 features or parts for 25 items, 2= at least 1 feature or part for 5 items, 1= at least 1 feature or part for 2 items

tasks.taskObjective: Student will be able to select objects or pictures of items when told the class to which the item belongs.
tasks.question: Can the student select objects or pictures of items when told the class to which the item belongs [e.g., Give me the animal(s)]?
tasks.examples: When shown pictures of a scissors, a shoe and a horse, and asked "Which one do you wear?;" the student will select the shoe.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can select at least 5 items from 4 classes and can select 2 or more items of a specified class from a display of at least 6 items, 3= at least 5 items from 4 classes, 2= at least 5 items from 2 classes, 1= at least 5 items from 1 class

tasks.taskName: Select two items from a larger set
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, the student will select two specified objects or pictures from a larger selection of objects on a table in front of the student.
tasks.question: Can the student select two specified objects or pictures from a larger selection of objects on a table in front of the student?
tasks.examples: When an assortment of 10 common objects or pictures are placed on a table, and the student is asked to "give me shoe and cup" student will pick up the cup and shoe
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can select 2 specified objects or pictures when given a display of 10 or more items, 1= can select 2 specified objects or pictures when given a display of at least 4 items

tasks.taskName: Select two items in sequence from a larger set
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, the student will select two specified objects or pictures, in the order requested, from a larger selection of pictures on a table in front of the student.
tasks.question: Can the student select two specified items, in the order requested, from a larger selection of pictures on a table in front of the student?
tasks.examples: When 10 common objects or pictures of items are placed on a table, and asked to "give me shoe and cup" student will pick up the pictures of the shoe and the cup in that order
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can select 2 specified items in order when given a display of 10 or more pictures, 1= can select 2 specified items in order when given a display of at least 4 pictures

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to select pictures of common community helpers in his environment.
tasks.question: Can the student select pictures of common community helpers in his environment?
tasks.examples: Teacher, police, fire fighter, physician, clerk
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= selects 4 or more community helpers, 3= 3 community helpers, 2= 2 community helpers, 1=1 community helper

tasks.taskName: Locate objects in larger, complex picture
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to locate pictures of objects within a larger, complex picture.
tasks.question: Can the student locate pictures of objects within a complex picture which contains a variety of other objects?
tasks.examples: Find all of the fish (same fish) in an underwater scene.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can find at least 3 of 4 items in a display which contains at least 10 other items, 1= can find at least 2 of 4 items in a display which contains at least 5 other items

tasks.taskName: Locate objects from parts of objects in larger, complex picture
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to locate objects when only shown parts of the objects within a larger, complex picture.
tasks.question: Can the student locate pictures of objects when only shown parts of the objects presented within a complex picture?
tasks.examples: Find all of the fish when only part of each fish may be visible (e.g., the head or the tail) in an underwater scene.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can find at least 3 of 4 items in a display which contains at least 10 other items, 1= can find at least 2 of 4 items in a display which contains at least 5 other items

tasks.taskObjective: The student will select appropriate pictures when the sound which is paired with that item is heard.
tasks.question: When listening to a tape recording of common sounds, or upon hearing a natural environmental sound and asked "What do you hear?," will the student select a picture of the item which makes the sound?
tasks.examples: Tools/machinery saw, drill.....Alert Sounds car horns, train whistles, ambulance/police sirens.....animals....even ts/activities.. birthday party, baseball game... vehicles car, train, airplanes
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 8 sounds, 3= at least 6 sounds, 2= at least 4 sounds, 1= at least 2 sounds

tasks.taskName: Selects all examples of an item
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to follow directions to select all the examples of a specified item (e.g., all the cats).
tasks.question: If you show the student an array or items, can he select all the examples of a specified item from that larger group of items?
tasks.examples: "Give me all the dogs"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 6 similar items from a total array of at least fifteen items, 3=3 items from an array of ten items, 2= 3 items from an array of at least six items, 1 = at least 2 similar items from a total array of at least four items

tasks.taskName: Select single items with two specified characteristics
tasks.taskObjective: Given a scene or a varied set of objects or pictures, the student will be able to select a specified item which has the two specified characteristics (e.g., "The big red ball," "The hot breakfast cereal").
tasks.question: Can the student select a specified item which has the two specified characteristics (e.g., "The big red ball," "The hot breakfast cereal") from a scene or a larger set of similar items?
tasks.examples: The big red ball, the hot breakfast cereal, the clothes you wear on your feet.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 two-component combinations, 3= 10 two- component combinations 2= 5 two-component combinations 1= 2 two-component combinations

tasks.taskName: Select set of items with a specified characteristic
tasks.taskObjective: Given a set of objects or pictures which vary only on a single characteristic, the student will be able to select all of the items which have a single specified characteristic (i.e., adjectives such as "The red ones").
tasks.question: Can the student select multiple items which have a specified characteristic from a larger set of similar items which vary along a single characteristic (i.e., adjectives)?
tasks.examples: The red ones, ones with holes, wrinkled/smooth ones, clean/dirty, new/used
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= selects at least 20 adjectives (including at least 3 colors, 2 shapes and 2 sizes), 3= at least 10 adjectives (at least 5 of which are not colors), 2= at least 5 adjectives (may be all colors), 1= can identify at least one adjective
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendices 5 & 6: Adjectives List & Colors and Shapes List

tasks.taskName: Select set of items with two specified characteristics
tasks.taskObjective: Given a varied set of objects or pictures, the student will be able to select all of the items which have the two specified characteristics (e.g., adjectives, parts or other features, function, or class of the item).
tasks.question: Can the student select multiple items which have two specified characteristics from a larger set of similar items which vary along those two characteristics (e.g., adjectives, parts or other features, function, or class of the item)?
tasks.examples: The big red ones, the green ones with holes, the big cars, the little shoes, the little green ones, red food items
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 two component combinations, 3= 10 two component combinations 2= 5 two component combinations 1= 2 two component combinations
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendices 5 & 6: Adjectives List & Colors and Shapes List

tasks.taskName: Follows a multiple component sequence instruction
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to select three items in a specified sequence.
tasks.question: Can the student select items in a specified sequence (e.g., "Touch the shoe, then touch the sock")?
tasks.examples: "Touch the shoe, then touch the sock"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= accurately selects 3 items in specified sequence after all the items are named, 1= accurately selects 2 items in specified sequence after both items are named

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to follow instructions which include selections involving prepositions.
tasks.question: Can the student follow directions which require selections involving prepositions?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 6 prepositions, 3= at least 5 prepositions, 2= at least 3 prepositions, 1= at least 2 prepositions

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to follow instructions which include selections involving pronouns.
tasks.question: Can the student follow directions which require selections involving pronouns?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 8 pronouns, 3= at least 4 pronouns, 2= at least 3, 1= at least 2 pronouns

tasks.taskName: Select pictures representing a location or an activity presented in a scene
tasks.taskObjective: Student will be able to select pictures of scenes or pictures of activities .
tasks.question: Can the student select pictures of specific locations and activities when presented with an array of pictures in which one of the pictures represent the location or activity?
tasks.examples: Fire in a house, fire truck, pulling the fire hose, spraying water on the house. Scenes of a beach, a birthday party, a picnic, a baseball game, a parade, a grocery store, a circus.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= selects at least 4 pictures depicting locations or activities, 1= selects at least 2 pictures depicting locations or activities

tasks.taskObjective: Student will be able to select pictures of faces depicting various emotions.
tasks.question: Can the student select pictures of faces depicting a variety of emotions?
tasks.examples: happy, sad, surprised, frightened, mad, scared
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 4 emotions, 3= at least 3 emotions, 2= at least 2 emotions, 1= at least 1 emotion

tasks.taskObjective: When the student is provided with a display of two items, then shown a third item which matches one of the two displayed items and told to either to "Find same," or to "Find different," he will select the corresponding item in the display.
tasks.question: Can the student select an item which is "Same" and "Different" from an array of two items when shown a third item which matches one of the two displayed items?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can select both "Same" and "Different" items when the two displayed items vary on only one characteristic, 1= can select both "Same" and "Different" items when the two displayed items vary on two or more characteristics

tasks.taskObjective: Student will be able to point to or select items which are non- examples of a specified category of items (e.g., not food, not yellow, not used to cook, does not have a tail).
tasks.question: Will the student point to or select items which do not meet a specified criterion (e.g., not food, not an animal, not green)?
tasks.examples: When student is looking at a book and is asked to point to something that is "not food," he points to a picture of a car.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 3 examples from 10 categories (can be related to functions, features, or classes of items) 3= 3 examples from at least 5 categories, 2= 3 examples from at least 3 categories, 1=3 examples from at least 2 categories (can be related to functions, features, or classes of items)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to select pictures representing a variety of social interactions (e.g., playing, arguing).
tasks.question: Can the student select pictures representing a variety of social interactions (e.qg., playing, arguing)?
tasks.examples: Embarrassed, arguing, fighting, talking, teasing, playing, working, practicing, busy, upset, friendly, stressed, funny.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= selects pictures representing at least 4 social interactions, 3= selects at least 3 social interactions, 2= selects at least 2 social interactions, 1= selects at least 1 social interaction

tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a motor activity with an object.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a motor action using an item/object when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Pretend to drink from a cup, roll a car down a ramp
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 actions with at least two different actions for each object, 3= 10 actions, 2=5 actions, 1=2 actions

tasks.taskName: Motor imitation using objects in a discrimination
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a motor activity requiring a discrimination of an object.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a motor action requiring a discrimination of an object when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: When the student has a pencil and a spoon & is shown putting a pencil in a cup, the student will do the same on request
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 actions & readily imitates novel actions, 3= 10 actions, 2=5 actions, 1=2 actions

tasks.taskName: Motor imitation of gross motor movement with verbal prompts
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a gross motor movement when provided with verbal prompts.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a gross motor action when asked to "Do this" and provided with verbal prompts?
tasks.examples: Jump up, clap hands
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 actions & readily imitates novel actions, 3= imitates any 10 actions, 2= imitates any 5 actions, 1= imitates any 2 actions

tasks.taskName: Imitation of leg and foot movements
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a gross motor activity involving foot and leg movements.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a gross motor action involving foot and leg movements when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Stomp foot
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 actions & readily imitates novel actions, 3= 10 actions, 2=5 actions, 1=2 actions
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendix 11: Imitative Skills List Note: Some of the skills exhibited in D3 may also be skills measured in Tasks D4 - D10 that measure more specific motor imitation skills

tasks.taskName: Imitation of arm and hand movements
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a gross motor activity involving arm and hand movements.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a gross motor action involving arm and hand movements when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Raise and lower arms at side
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 actions & readily imitates novel actions, 3= 10 actions, 2=5 actions, 1=2 actions

tasks.taskName: Imitation discriminating static and kinetic motor movements
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate similar actions that require him to discriminate whether the action requires either a static (held position) or a kinetic (movement) motor movement.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate both actions that require him to demonstrate holding a static position and those that require him to imitate a similar action that requires repeated movement when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Tap table with a hand vs. hold the hand on table, clap hands vs. holding palms together, tap foot on a circle vs. place and hold foot on the circle.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 pairs of actions & readily imitates novel actions, 3= imitates any 10 pairs of actions, 2= imitates any 5 pairs of actions, 1= imitates any 2 pairs of similar actions where one response in the pair involves movement and the other is a static response.
tasks.protocolNotes: New. See Appendix 11: Imitative Skills List

tasks.taskObjective: The student will imitate actions when any of a variety of instructions are used to indicate that he is to imitate an action.
tasks.question: Can the student imitate actions when the instructions are varied?
tasks.examples: Will imitate a model when asked to "Watch me, Your turn," "Do what I do," "Follow me," "You try it," "My turn, Now you do it," or "Do like this"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= imitates known actions when given any one of 4 different instructions to imitate, 1= imitates known actions when given any one of at least of 2 different instructions to imitate

tasks.taskName: Imitation of gross motor actions modeled in a mirror
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate gross motor movements that he observes being modeled by others in a mirror.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate gross motor movements that he observes being modeled by others in a mirror when asked to "Do this" ?
tasks.examples: Put hand on head, clap hands, rub stomach, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 actions & readily imitates novel actions, 3= imitates any 10 actions, 2= imitates any 5 actions, 1= imitates any 2 actions
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendix 11: Imitative Skills List - New

tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a gross motor activity involving head movements.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a gross motor action involving head movements when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Shake head from side to side
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= imitates 3 actions, 1= one action

tasks.taskName: Imitation of mouth and tongue movements
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a motor activity involving mouth and tongue movements.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a motor action involving his mouth and tongue when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Stick out tongue
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= imitates 4 actions, 1= 2 actions

tasks.taskName: Imitation of facial/oral motor movements modeled in a mirror
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate facial/oral motor movements that he observes being modeled by others in a mirror.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate facial/oral motor movements that he observes being modeled by others in a mirror when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Open mouth, squeeze lips together, stick out tongue, move tongue side-to-side, lips to blowing position, puffy cheeks, blinking, raising eyebrows.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 6 facial/oral motor movements including those that require repeated movement and those that require a held position (static), 3= imitates any 6 actions, 2= imitates any 4 actions, 1= imitates any 2 facial/oral motor actions
tasks.protocolNotes: New. See Appendix 11: Imitative Skills List

tasks.taskName: Motor imitation of fine motor movement
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a fine motor activity.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a fine motor action when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Touch tips of index fingers together
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 actions & readily imitates novel actions, 3= 10 actions, 2=5 actions, 1=2 actions

tasks.taskName: Imitation of touching objects in sequence
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate touching objects in a sequence at the same time as a person modeling the sequence.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate touching objects in a sequence switching to touch the next item when the model touches that item?
tasks.examples: With a set of 4 identically arranged objects, student matches model when he touches a car, then shoe, then cup, then horse.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can imitate any sequence of touching 4 of 6 items, 1=can imitate any sequence of touching 2 of 4 items.

tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate both short and sustained blowing actions when modeled by others.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate both short and sustained blowing actions when modeled by others when asked to "Do this" ?
tasks.examples: Simple blowing action and a sustained 2 second blowing action.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= imitates both a short and a sustained blowing action of at least 2 seconds duration, 1= can imitate either a short or an extended blowing action

tasks.taskName: Imitate speed of an ongoing action with objects
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a motor activity involving manipulating an object matching the speed of the ongoing model.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a motor action involving the manipulation of an object matching the speed of an ongoing model when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Imitates the speed of an ongoing model moving an object (e.g., shaking a tambourine quickly or slowly at the same time a model of the action is being demonstrated)
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily imitates actions matching the speed of the ongoing model, 1= requires only verbal prompts to match the speed of the ongoing model

tasks.taskName: Imitate speed of a recently modeled action with objects
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a motor activity involving manipulating an object matching the speed of a recently modeled action.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a motor action involving the manipulation of an object matching the speed of a recently modeled action when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Immediately following a demonstration of an action with an object, student imitates the modeled action matching the speed of the model moving the object (e.g., shaking a tambourine quickly or slowly)
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily imitates actions with objects matching the speed of the action immediately following a demonstration, 1= requires only one verbal prompt to match the speed of the action immediately following a demonstration

tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a gross motor activity matching the speed of the model.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a gross motor action matching the speed of the model when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Slowly or quickly raise arms at side
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily imitates actions matching the speed of the model, 1= requires only verbal prompts to match the speed of the model

tasks.taskName: Imitation of touching objects in sequence following a model
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate touching objects in a sequence after the sequence of items to be touched has been demonstrated.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate touching objects in a sequence after the sequence of items to be touched has been demonstrated?
tasks.examples: With a set of 4 objects, student watches model as he touches a car, a shoe, a cup, then a horse. The student then touches those items in the same sequence.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can imitate touching any sequence of touching 4 of 6 items immediately following a demonstration, 1= can imitate touching any sequence of touching 2 of 4 items immediately following a demonstration.

tasks.taskName: Imitation of a sequence of actions switching with model
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a sequence of motor actions along with a model immediately switching from one action to another following the lead of the model.
tasks.question: When asked to "Do this," will the student imitate a sequence of motor actions along with a model immediately switching from one action to another following the lead of the model?
tasks.examples: Clap hands, shake hands, rub hands, then tap thighs, immediately changing from one action to another when a leader changes his actions
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can imitate a sequence of 6 different modeled actions within 10 seconds, 1= can imitate a sequence of 4 different modeled actions within 10 seconds

tasks.taskName: Imitation of a sequence of actions
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a sequence of motor activities.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a sequence of motor actions when asked to "Do this" followed by a model of a sequence of actions?
tasks.examples: Clap hands then tap thighs
