tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 sequences of two actions & readily imitates novel sequences , 3= 10 sequences of two actions, 2= 5 sequences of two actions, 1= 2 sequences of two actions after a sequence has been modeled

tasks.taskName: Imitation of the intensity of an action
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a gross motor activity matching the intensity of the model.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a gross motor action matching the intensity of the model when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Tap a table with a hard tap vs. a soft tap, clap hands hard vs soft clap (Note that slow or fast claps can be either hard or soft)
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily imitates actions matching the intensity of the model, 1= requires only verbal prompts to match the intensity of the model

tasks.taskName: Imitation of the number of repetitions of a motor movement
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a motor movement for the same number of repetitions as was just modeled.
tasks.question: Following a demonstration by a model, will the student imitate the same number of repetitions of an action when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: Tap a drum with a stick once vs. three times
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= imitates any number of up to three repetitions of a response without prompts 1= imitates any number of up to three repetitions of a response when provided with only verbal or gestural prompts

tasks.taskName: Simultaneous imitation of motor movement and a vocalization
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a motor movement along with a corresponding vocalization.
tasks.question: When asked to "Do this" then shown a demonstration that combines an action and a vocalization, will the student imitate the same combination of motor action and vocalization?
tasks.examples: Wave raised arms from side to side while saying "Swish, swish, swish." Move arms like cradling a baby while saying "Wa, wa, wa"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= imitates up to three repetitions of at least 4 different motor and vocal response combinations without prompts 1= imitates at least one motor and vocal response combination without prompts

tasks.taskName: Motor imitation sequence using multiple objects
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a sequence of actions using multiple objects.
tasks.question: Will the student imitate a sequence of actions using multiple objects when asked to "Do this"?
tasks.examples: When a toy truck, a small box and a red, blue, yellow and a white block are present, the student imitates a sequence of putting the blue block on top of the white block then places the red block in the box and the yellow block in the back of the truck.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can replicate at least 6 different sequences of at least three actions involving 4 objects with the original model remaining visible, 1= can replicate at least 6 different sequences of at least two actions involving 4 objects with the original model remaining visible

tasks.taskName: Imitates motor movement without a direct verbal prompt
tasks.taskObjective: Without being told to imitate each action, student will imitate gross motor actions modeled by an individual, for the social recognition of being able to match the actions.
tasks.question: Does the student imitate the gross motor actions of others, for only the personal satisfaction or for the social recognition of being able to match the actions?
tasks.examples: Make a series of facial and head movements that are being done by others.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 actions & readily imitates novel actions, 3= 10 actions, 2= 5 actions, 1= 2 actions

tasks.taskName: Spontaneously imitates the actions of others
tasks.taskObjective: Student will spontaneously imitate a gross motor activity modeled by an individual who is not standing directly in front of the student.
tasks.question: Does the student spontaneously imitate the actions of others who are not directly in front of him (i.e., without having to be prompted or told to imitate the action)?
tasks.examples: Watches others and does what others do (e.g., all hop, clap, stand, sit, put hands on hips).
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 actions & readily imitates novel actions (not necessary to be a sequence of 10) , 3= 10 actions, 2=5 actions, 1= 2 actions

tasks.taskObjective: Upon request or when labeling his own actions, student will be able to demonstrate actions which he observed several hours earlier in the day.
tasks.question: Does the student imitate actions which he observed earlier in the day either spontaneously while labeling his behavior, or upon request?
tasks.examples: "This is what the lion did" or "show me how Cinderella scrubbed the floor"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= label and imitate numerous actions observed 4 hours ago, 3= label and imitate after 1 hour, 2= label and imitate after 10 minutes, 1= upon request, 1 action after 5 minutes

tasks.taskObjective: The student will imitate a sound when you say ,"Say
tasks.question: Can the student imitate sounds upon request?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= readily and accurately imitates almost any sound, 3= 15 sounds, 2=5 sounds, 1= 2 sounds

tasks.taskName: Imitates sequence of single sounds switching with a model
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to repeat a series of individual sounds presented in quick succession.
tasks.question: Is the student able to repeat a sequence of sounds immediately after they are presented in a one-after-the-other manner?
tasks.examples: Child quickly repeats each sound presented in rapid succession (e.g., "May", "Moe", "Me", "ah", "buh", "ee", "oh" )
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can repeat at least 10 separate sounds in 15 seconds, 1= can repeat 5 separate sounds in 10 seconds

tasks.taskObjective: When a word is modeled for the student, he will be able to imitate the initial sounds of that word.
tasks.question: Can the student imitate the initial sounds of words which are modeled to them?
tasks.examples: For "bat" says "ba" For "shoe" says "sh" For "apple" says "ap" For "up" says "uh"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= readily and accurately imitates at least the first sound of almost any word, 3= 15 sounds, 2=5 sounds, 1= 2 sounds

tasks.taskName: Imitation of multiple separate sound combinations
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to repeat a variety of separate sounds in combination in which the student must attend to both sounds.
tasks.question: Is the student able to repeat his known sounds in a variety of combinations in which the sounds are presented?
tasks.examples: Says "ma" "ma" vs. "ma" "me" vs. "ma" "moe", says "ee" "0" vs. "ee" "ee" vs. "ee" "ah"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can repeat at least 4 pairs of sound combinations for at least 4 starting sounds, 1= can repeat at least 3 pairs of sound combinations for at least 2 starting sounds

tasks.taskName: Imitation of short & fast vs. elongated/slow sounds
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to repeat sounds matching the speed of the presented sound.
tasks.question: If a sound is presented in a deliberately slow or fast manner, is the child able to match the speed that sounds are said to him?
tasks.examples: Says "mm" vs "mmmmm"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily imitates sounds matching the speed of the model, 1= requires only gestural prompts to match the speed of the model

tasks.taskName: Imitation of the number of repetitions of a sound
tasks.taskObjective: Upon request, student will imitate a sound for the same number of repetitions as was just modeled.
tasks.question: Following a demonstration by a model, will the student imitate the same number of repetitions of a sound when asked to "Say (sound)"?
tasks.examples: Say "ah" once vs. "ah" "ah" "ah"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= imitates any number of up to three repetitions of a sound without prompts 1= imitates any number of up to three repetitions of a sound when provided with only gestural prompts

tasks.taskName: Imitation of a held sound to a second sound
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to repeat sound combinations in which the model requires the student to hold or elongate the first sound and smoothly transition to a second sound (not merely say two separate sounds).
tasks.question: Is the student able to repeat a combination of sounds that requires the student to hold or elongate the first sound and smoothly transition to a second sound (not merely say two separate sounds)?
tasks.examples: Says "mmmeeeee" smoothly transitioning from the "mm" sound to the "eee" sound (not two independent sounds "mm".."ee"), "aaaaammmm" as in an elongated "am"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can smoothly switch between at least 4 held/ elongated sounds to at least 4 other sounds, 1= can smoothly switch between at least 2 held/elongated sounds to at least 2 other sounds

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to repeat sound combinations in which the model requires the student to repeat consonant- vowel and vowel consonant combinations (e.g., "eat," "up," "go," "me")
tasks.question: Is the student able to able to repeat simple sound combinations involving a single vowel and a consonant?
tasks.examples: up, on, in, am, ma, my, moo
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can repeat at least 3 vowel- consonant and 3 consonant- vowel sound combinations without breaks between the two sounds, 1= can repeat at least 3 vowel- consonant or consonant-vowel sound combinations without breaks between the two sounds

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to repeat sound combinations in which the model requires the student to repeat consonant- vowel-consonant-vowel combinations (e.g., "mama," "dada," "peepee," "meme")
tasks.question: Is the student able to repeat sound combinations in which the model requires the student to repeat consonant- vowel- consonant-vowel combinations?
tasks.examples: "mama," "dada," "pee pee," "me me," "boo boo," "bye bye"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can repeat at least 6 consonant-vowel- consonant- vowel sound combinations without breaks between the sounds, 1= can repeat at least 3 consonant- vowel- consonant-vowel sound combinations without breaks between the sounds

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to repeat sound combinations (words) in which the model requires the student to repeat consonant- vowel-consonant combinations (e.g., "mom," "dad," "top," "pig")
tasks.question: Is the student able to repeat sound combinations (words) in which the model requires the student to repeat consonant- vowel- consonant combinations?
tasks.examples: "mom," "dad," "top," "hat," "cat," "sit," "hop," "pig"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can repeat at least 12 consonant-vowel- consonant sound combinations (words) without breaks between the sounds, 1= can repeat at least 3 consonant-vowel- consonant sound combinations (words) without breaks between the sounds

tasks.taskObjective: When a word which contains consonant blends are modeled for the student, he will be able to accurately imitate the words.
tasks.question: Can the student imitate words which include consonant blends (e.g., STReet, againST, SPLash, riNG)?
tasks.examples: 2 consonant blends "St", & 3 consonant blends npr
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= readily and accurately imitates almost any word with consonant blends in any position, 3= 15 words with consonant blends can be accurately imitated, 2=5 words, 1= 2 words

tasks.taskObjective: The student will imitate a word when you say ,"Say ___"
tasks.question: Can the student imitate words upon request (including the final sounds of the word)?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= readily and accurately imitates almost any word , 3= closely approximates 15 words, 2= closely approximates 5 words, 1= closely approximates 2 words

tasks.taskObjective: The student will imitate a phrase when you say ,"Say
tasks.question: Can the student imitate phrases upon request?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= readily and accurately imitates phrases of 6 or more words , 3= 4- word phrases, 2= 3-word phrases, 1=2-word phrases

tasks.taskName: Imitation of number sequences on request
tasks.taskObjective: The student will imitate a sequence of numbers when you say ,"Say ___"
tasks.question: Can the student imitate a sequence of numbers upon request (e.g., a phone number)?
tasks.examples: Repeats a phone number
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= readily and accurately imitates sequence of 7 or more numbers , 3=4 numbers, 2= 3 numbers, 1= 2 numbers

tasks.taskName: Imitation of short & fast vs. elongated/slow words
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to repeat words matching the speed of the presented word.
tasks.question: If a word is presented in a deliberately slow or fast manner, will the child match the speed that words are said to him?
tasks.examples: Says the word 'Movie' at a typical speed, slowly asin "mooooveeee" and quickly
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can imitate saying words both at a faster and slower than a normal rate of speaking, 1= can imitate saying words at a faster or slower than normal rate of speaking

tasks.taskName: Imitation of loud vs. soft sounds and words
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to repeat words matching the volume of the presented word.
tasks.question: If a word is presented in a deliberately loud or quiet (whispered) manner, will the child match the volume that words are said to him?
tasks.examples: Says "apple" in a loud voice vs. quiet voice (e.g., whispers)
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily imitates sounds or words matching the volume of the model, 1= requires only gestural prompts to match the volume of the model

tasks.taskName: Imitation of low vs. high sounds and words
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to repeat words matching the pitch/tone of the presented word.
tasks.question: If a word is presented in a deliberately high or low pitched voice, will the child match the pitch/tone that words are said to him?
tasks.examples: Says "apple" in a high pitched voice vs. a low pitched voice
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily imitates sounds or words matching the pitch/tone of the model, 1= requires only gestural prompts to match the pitch/tone of the model

tasks.taskName: Repeat short message to another person
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to go to a person and repeat a short statement that he was told to say to the person.
tasks.question: Is the student able to deliver a short message to others?
tasks.examples: Mom asks child to tell his Dad "I want pizza" and child walks to his Dad and says "I want pizza"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can repeat a three-word phrase after going at least ten feet to deliver the message, 1= can repeat a two-word phrase after going at least five feet to deliver the message

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously imitate words.
tasks.question: Does the child spontaneously imitate words?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= accurately imitates at least 20 words per day, 3= 15 words, 2=5 words, 1= 2 words per day

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously imitate phrases.
tasks.question: Does the child spontaneously imitate phrases?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= accurately imitates phrases of 6 or more words at least 3 times per day , 3= 4-word phrases 3 times per day, 2= 3-word phrases 3 times per day, 1 =2-word phrases at least 3 times per day

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to specifically indicate items and activities which he wants by pointing to, pulling to, or standing by the particular items or activities (without using words or sign language).
tasks.question: Does the student indicate specific items and activities which he wants by pointing to, pulling to, or standing by the particular items and activities (without using words or sign language)?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= a total of at least 5 requests per day which include at least 3 different items or activities, 1= requests 1 item or activity at least once per day
tasks.protocolNotes: Note: This task should also be scored a "2" if the student spontaneously requests at least 3 items or activties (as defined in F5) at least 5 times per day.

tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask for what he wants when the reinforcer is present and a word or a sign given.
tasks.question: If you ask "What do you want?" with the reinforcer present and an imitative prompt (word or a sign) will the student ask for the item?
tasks.examples: With an apple present, instructor says "What do you want?....apple" student then signs (ASL) or says "apple"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=10 or more items or activities, 3=6 items or activities, 2=4 items or activities, 1=1 item or activity

tasks.taskName: Requesting with the reinforcer present and when asked "What do you want?"
tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask for what he wants with the reinforcer present using either words or signs.
tasks.question: Does the student ask for reinforcing items or events using either words or signs?
tasks.examples: With an apple present, instructor asks "What do you want?" then the student signs (ASL) or says "apple"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=10 or more items or activities, 3=6 items or activities, 2=4 items or activities, 1=1 item or activity

tasks.taskName: Requesting when asked "What do you want?"
tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask for items that he wants with no reinforcers present.
tasks.question: If you ask "What do you want," will the student ask for an item or an activity?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=10 or more items or activities, 3=6 items or activities, 2=4 items or activities, 1=2 items or activities

tasks.taskName: Spontaneous requests with items present (No prompts)
tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously ask for at least 10 items that he wants using a specific response (Spoken word or with an American Sign Language sign) when the items are present.
tasks.question: How many specific items or activities can the student spontaneously ask for using a specific response (Spoken word or with an American Sign Language sign) when the items are present?
tasks.examples: Student spontaneously asks for a cookie when the cookie is present and without having been asked what he wants.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 10 or more specific items or activities when the items or items associated with the activity are present, 3= 6 specific items or activities, 2= 4 specific items or activities, 1= 2 specific items or activities (items present)

tasks.taskName: Spontaneous requests with items not present (No prompts)
tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously ask for at least 10 items that he wants using a specific response (Spoken word or with an American Sign Language sign) when the items are not present.
tasks.question: How many specific items or activities can the student spontaneously ask for using a specific response (Spoken word or with an American Sign Language sign) when the items are not present?
tasks.examples: Student spontaneously asks for a cookie when the cookie is not present and without having been asked what he wants.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 10 or more specific items or activities when the items or items associated with the activity are not present, 3= 6 specific items or activities, 2= 4 specific items or activities, 1= 2 specific items or activities (items not present)
tasks.protocolNotes: New. Note: Items F2 - F5 should each be scored a "4" if the student receives a score of "4" on this task.

tasks.taskObjective: The student will make eye contact when asking a person for items, actions or information.
tasks.question: Does the student look at people when he is asking for items, actions or information?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= makes eye contact with people at least 80% of the times that he makes requests , 1= makes eye contact with people at least 50% of the time that he makes requests

tasks.taskName: Request others to perform an action
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to ask others to perform specified actions.
tasks.question: Does the student ask others to perform specified actions?
tasks.examples: Ask others to "come" with them, "stand up," "sing," "open," "push," "up" (as in pick up), "Help me put this away," "Show me how you do that."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can request 10 or more different actions, 3= 6 actions, 2= 3 actions, 1= requests 1 action

tasks.taskName: Requests missing items needed for a task
tasks.taskObjective: When only given some of the items necessary to do an activity, the student will ask for the missing item.
tasks.question: When an item is needed to complete a task, does the student ask for the missing item?
tasks.examples: Given a bowl of cereal without a spoon, given a cup without juice
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=10 or more, 3= at least 6, 2= at least 3, 1= can ask for 1 missing item

tasks.taskName: Requests with head movements or by saying Yes/No
tasks.taskObjective: Student will be able to ask for or reject offered items and activities using head movements to specify "Yes" or "No."
tasks.question: Can the student indicate he wants or does not want an item or activity by saying or using head movements to specify "Yes" or "No"?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= both yes and no, 1= only one of the two

tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask questions in a sentence form to obtain items, actions, or information.
tasks.question: Can the student ask for items, actions, or information using a sentence?
tasks.examples: I would like some juice, I need a pencil, can I have popcorn, give me a banana, I want a ride, juice please
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= usually uses three or more words to ask for items or activities, 1= sometimes uses three or more words to ask for items or activities

tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask for help when he needs assistance.
tasks.question: Can the student ask for help (e.g., "Help me")?
tasks.examples: "Help," "Help me with this," "Turn the book so I can see it," "fix (adjust) my coat"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= asks for help in a wide variety of situations, 1= asks for help in only 1 or 2 specific situations (e.g., tie shoes, open containers)

tasks.taskName: Acquires novel requests without intensive training
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to acquire new requests for many new objects, actions, or information after being required to request those items less than five times.
tasks.question: Is the student able to acquire new requests for many new objects, actions, or information after being required to request those items less than five times?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily learns new requests without direct training, 1= readily able to learn new requests for objects, actions, or information when asked to request the items less than five times

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to ask others to attend to his actions.
tasks.question: Does the student ask others to attend to his actions (e.g., "Mommy, look at me," "Watch this")?
tasks.examples: Call a person's name to get attention, raise hand, say "Mommy, look at me," "Watch this," "Look what I did"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=10 or more requests per day, 3= 6 request per day, 2=4 request per day, 1=2 requests per day

tasks.taskName: Request others to remove an item or stop an activity
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to ask others to remove an item or stop an activity.
tasks.question: Can the student ask others to remove an item or stop activity?
tasks.examples: Ask others to turn off music, a fan, to stop running, "let go."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can do spontaneously, 1= can do in contrived situations

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to ask for items using adjectives (e.g., big horse).
tasks.question: Can the student ask for items using adjectives (e.g., big horse)?
tasks.examples: While playing with a toy farm set the student asks for the "big horse"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= Spontaneously uses at least 4 adjectives with a noun when requesting an item, 1= uses at least 2 adjectives with or without a noun in contrived situations

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to ask for items using prepositions (e.g., in the box).
tasks.question: Can the student ask for items using prepositions (e.g., in the box)?
tasks.examples: While playing with dolls, the student asks for a doll to be put "in the cradle"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= Spontaneously uses at least 4 prepositions with a noun when requesting an item, 1= uses at least 2 prepositions with or without a noun in contrived situations

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to ask for items or actions which he may be able to obtain in the future.
tasks.question: Does the student ask for items or actions which he may want to obtain in the future?
tasks.examples: In the morning the student asks to watch a video tape after lunch.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= Spontaneously requests items or activities one or more days in advance, 1= Spontaneously requests to have items or participate in activities after completion of an activity or later in the day

tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask questions to obtain information.
tasks.question: Does the student ask for information using "What" questions?
tasks.examples: Student sees an unfamiliar object and asks "What is it?" or "What does it do?"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously asks "What" questions in non-training situations when unknown items are present, 1=can ask "What" questions when unknown items are presented in training situations (or otherwise prompted)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask questions to obtain information.
tasks.question: Does the student ask for information using "Where" questions?
tasks.examples: Parent says "We're going out to eat" and student asks "Where are we going?" Parent says "Get your shoes" and student asks "Where are my shoes?"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously asks "Where" questions in non-training situations when unknown items or situations are present, 1=can ask "Where" questions when unknown items or situations are presented in training situations (or otherwise prompted)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask questions to obtain information.
tasks.question: Does the student ask for information using "Who" or "Whose" questions?
tasks.examples: "Whose turn?," "Whose shoe is this?," "Who is it?"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously asks "Who" questions in non-training situations when unknown items are present, 1= can ask "Who" questions when unknown items are presented in training situations (or otherwise prompted)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to ask for actions using adverbs (e.g., push me fast, walk quietly).
tasks.question: Can the student ask for actions using adverbs (e.g., push me fast, walk quietly)?
tasks.examples: While riding in a wagon the student says "push me fast," "Let's talk quietly," "throw it harder"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= Spontaneously uses at least 4 adverbs with a noun when requesting an action, 1= uses at least 2 adverbs with or without a action in contrived situations

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to ask for items using pronouns (e.g., | want your hat).
tasks.question: Can the student ask for items using pronouns (e.g., | want your hat)?
tasks.examples: While playing dress up, the student says "l want your hat"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= Spontaneously uses at least 4 pronouns with a noun when requesting an item, 1= uses at least 2 pronouns with or without a noun in contrived situations

tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask questions to obtain information.
tasks.question: Does the student ask for information using "Which" questions?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously asks "Which" questions in non-training situations when unknown items are present, 1= can ask "Which" questions when unknown items are presented in training situations (or otherwise prompted)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask questions to obtain information.
tasks.question: Does the student ask for information using "When" questions?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously asks "When" questions in non-training situations when unknown items are present, 1=can ask "When" questions when unknown items are presented in training situations (or otherwise prompted)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask questions to obtain information.
tasks.question: Does the student ask for information using "How" questions?
tasks.examples: "Show me how you do that"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously asks "How" questions in non-training situations when unknown items are present, 1=can ask "How" questions when unknown items are presented in training situations (or otherwise prompted)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask questions to obtain information.
tasks.question: Does the student ask for information using questions?
tasks.examples: Do..., will..., can..., does... Can (I get shoes at a gas station)
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously uses at least 2 forms of non "Wh"-type of questions, 1= spontaneously uses at least 1 form of non-"Wh" question

tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask questions to obtain information.
tasks.question: Does the student ask for information using "Why" questions?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously asks "Why" questions in non-training situations when unknown items are present, 1=can ask "Why" questions when unknown items are presented in training situations (or otherwise prompted)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously request objects, actions, or information throughout the day.
tasks.question: Does the student spontaneously request objects, actions, or information throughout the day?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously requests objects, actions, or information at least 20 times per day, 1= spontaneously requests objects, actions, or information at least 10 times per day

tasks.taskObjective: The student will label reinforcing items.
tasks.question: If you ask "What is that?" with one of his reinforcing items present, will the student identify the item?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=10 or more labels, 3=6 labels, 2=4 labels, 1=2 labels

tasks.taskObjective: The student will label at least 100 objects which are commonly found in his environment.
tasks.question: If you ask "What is that?" with a common item present, will the student identify the item?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=100 or more labels of items and can identify several different examples (including novel examples) of most of those items, 3=50 labels of at least one example of the item, 2=10 labels, 1=5 labels
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendix 3: Receptive and Label List Note that objects selected should be ones that the student hears the names of and interacts with on a frequent basis.

tasks.taskName: Labels common people (actual individuals, not professionals)
tasks.taskObjective: The student will label people in his environment.
tasks.question: If you ask "Who is this?" with the person present, will the student identify the person?
tasks.examples: Mom, Dad, siblings (Rachel), friends (Jason, Emily)
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=10 or more people, 3=6 people, 2= 4 people, 1= 2 people

tasks.taskObjective: The student will label at least 100 pictures of items which are commonly found in his environment.
tasks.question: If you ask "What is that?" when shown a picture of a common item, will the student identify the item?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 100 or more labels of pictures of items and can identify several different examples (including novel examples) of most of those items, 3=50 labels of at least one example of the item, 2=10 labels, 1=5 labels
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendix 3: Receptive and Label List

tasks.taskObjective: The student will label common body parts on himself or others.
tasks.question: Can the student label body parts on himself or others?
tasks.examples: Labels nose, eyes, hair on himself, a doll, another person, or a picture of a person
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can label 20 or more body parts on himself or others, 3=10 body parts, 2=5 body parts, 1= at least 2 body parts on himself or others

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label clothing items.
tasks.question: Can the student label pieces of clothing?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= labels 4 or more clothing items, 1= labels 2 clothing items

tasks.taskObjective: The student will label common actions.
tasks.question: If you ask "What is he doing?" in the presence of an ongoing action, will the student identify the action?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more labels of actions and can identify several different examples (including novel examples) of most of those actions, 3=10 actions, 2=5 actions, 1=2 actions
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendix 8: Actions and Verbs List

tasks.taskObjective: The student will label pictures of common actions.
tasks.question: If you ask "What is he doing?" when shown a picture of an action, will the student identify the action?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more labels of pictures of actions and can identify several different examples (including novel examples) of most of those actions, 3= 10 actions, 2=5 actions, 1=2 actions
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendix 8: Actions and Verbs List

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label known items in quick succession.
tasks.question: Is the student able to label known items when presented items in a one- after-the-other manner?
tasks.examples: When asked to label items on a worksheet or in a book, child can label shoe, cup, and apple in rapid succession. Can quickly label colors, numbers, letters, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can sequentially label at least 10 known items in 15 seconds, 1= can label 5 separate known items in 10 seconds

tasks.taskName: Acquires novel labels without intensive training
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to acquire labels for many new common items or pictures of items after only hearing the name of those items used by others (no direct training).
tasks.question: Is the student able to acquire labels for many new common items or pictures of items after only hearing the name of those items used by others (no direct training)?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily learns the names of many new items only from hearing the name of those items used by others (no direct training), 1= readily able to learn labels for common items when asked to name the items less than five times

tasks.taskName: Labels items using a carrier phrase
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use a variety of carrier phrases when labeling items, and will frequently use those carrier phrases without prompting.
tasks.question: Does the student use a variety of carrier phrases when labeling items; and if so, does the student frequently use those carrier phrases without prompting?
tasks.examples: "It's an airplane"; "Look, an airplane"; "I see an airplane"; "There goes an airplane"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= when spontaneously labeling items, the student will include a carrier phrase at least half of all spontaneous labels and uses at least 2 different carrier phrases, 1= when prompted, the student can label items using at least 2 different phrases

tasks.taskName: Labels parts or features of objects
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label the parts or features of objects.
tasks.question: Can the student label the parts or features of objects?
tasks.examples: While looking at a picture of a car, the student labels the door, wheel, and window
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 3 parts or features of 10 or more objects, 3= 3 parts or features of 4 objects, 2= 2 parts or features of 4 objects, 1= 2 parts or features of 2 objects

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use adjectives that describe objects.
tasks.question: Can the student identify properties of objects (color, size, shape, texture, length, etc.)?
tasks.examples: The truck is red; This shoe is ... big/ little; This water is ... hot/cold
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= labels using at least 20 adjectives (including at least 3 colors, 2 shapes and 2 sizes), 3= at least 10 adjectives (5 of which are not colors), 2= at least 5 adjectives (may be all colors), 1= can identify at least one adjective
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendices 5 & 6: Adjectives List & Colors and Shapes List

tasks.taskObjective: When presented with an array of items or pictures and then shown another item or picture and asked, "What goes with this?," the student will be able to label one of the items which is associated with the item being shown (e.g., says "chair" when shown picture of a table and a set of pictures including a chair, shoe and a set of keys).
tasks.question: When given a display of objects or pictures and shown a different item and asked, "What goes with this?," can the student name an item from the display which is used with the item being presented (e.g., says "bat" when shown a ball and pictures of a bat, shoe and a pillow)?
tasks.examples: bat and a ball, cup and juice, socks and shoes, pillow and bed
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can label at least 2 related pictures for 20 or more items, 3= 2 related pictures for 10 items, 2= 1 related picture for 10 items, 1= can label at least 1 related picture for 5 items

tasks.taskName: Labels item when told its function
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label items when only told the function of the item.
tasks.question: In the presence of items or pictures of items, can the student label items when only told the function of the item?
tasks.examples: When shown pictures of scissors, a shoe and a horse, and asked "what do you cut with?; the student will say, "scissors."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= label a total of at least 25 items including at least 4 examples of at least 6 functions, 3= at least 10 items, 2= at least 5 items, 1=2 items

tasks.taskName: Labels item when told one of its features
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label items when only told the feature of the item.
tasks.question: In the presence of items or pictures of items, can the student label items when only told the feature of the item?
tasks.examples: When shown pictures of scissors, a shoe and a horse, and told "it has a tail" or "it has legs" the student will say, "horse."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= label a total of at least 25 items including at least 2 examples of at least 6 features, 3= at least 10 items, 2= at least 5 items, 1=2 items

tasks.taskName: Labels item when told its class
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label items when only told the class of the item.
tasks.question: In the presence of several items or pictures of items, can the student label items when only told the class of the item?
tasks.examples: When shown pictures of scissors, a shirt and a horse, and asked "which one is clothing?; the student will say, "shirt."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 5 items from 4 classes, 3= at least 5 items from 3 classes, 2= at least 5 items from 2 classes, 1= at least 5 items from 1 class

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label a set of items given to him.
tasks.question: Can the student identify two or more objects presented together?
tasks.examples: When shown two pictures of animals and asked "What are these?" the student will say "Cat and dog"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 20 pairs of items, 3= at least 10 pairs of items, 2= at least 5 pairs of items, 1= at least 2 pairs of items.
tasks.protocolNotes: Note: "and" is not required between the names of the items

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label more than one item presented on a picture card.
tasks.question: Can the student identify two or more objects presented on a picture card?
tasks.examples: When shown a picture of a playground the student will say, "Swing, slide" ("and" not required)
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 20 pairs of items, 3= at least 10 pairs of items, 2= at least 5 pairs of items, 1= at least 2 pairs of items.

tasks.taskName: Labels two- component with carrier phrase
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use a variety of carrier phrases when labeling multiple items, and will frequently use those carrier phrases without prompting.
tasks.question: Does the student use a variety of carrier phrases when labeling multiple items, and if so, does the student frequently use those carrier phrases without prompting?
tasks.examples: "It's an airplane and a helicopter"; "Look, an airplane and a helicopter"; "I see an airplane and a helicopter"; "There goes an airplane and a helicopter"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= when spontaneously labeling items, the student will include a carrier phrase for at least half of all spontaneous labels and uses at least 2 different carrier phrases, 1= when prompted, the student can label items using at least 2 different phrases

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label a noun and a verb in combination.
tasks.question: Can the student identify an object and the action performed with the object?
tasks.examples: When rolling a ball, the student can say "Roll ball"; upon seeing a picture of a girl riding a bike in a park, the student says, "ride bike."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= uses at least 10 verbs with a variety of nouns, 3= uses at least 5 verbs with a variety of nouns, 2= at least 5 noun-verb pairs, 1= at least 2 noun-verb pairs.

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label an adjective and a noun in combination.
tasks.question: Can the student identify an object and one property of the object?
tasks.examples: When presented with a red ball the student will say, "Red ball."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= uses at least 10 adjectives with a variety of nouns, 3= at least 5 adjectives with a variety of nouns, 2= at least 5 noun-adjective pairs, 1= at least 2 noun-adjective pairs

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer "Yes" or "No" or move his head to indicate "Yes" or "No" to identify the name of an item or to identify if an item or activity meets a pre- specified criterion.
tasks.question: Can the student say or move his head "Yes" or "No" to identify the name of an item being shown to him or to indicate whether the item meets a pre-specified criterion?
tasks.examples: When presented with a picture of a cat and asked "Is this a dog?" the student will move his head to indicate "no"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= yes & no regarding features of items present, 1= yes & no with regard to the label of items present

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label the function of items when asked "What do you do with this?"
tasks.question: When shown an item or picture of an item, can the student identify the function of the item?
tasks.examples: When shown a picture of a cup and asked "what do you do with a cup?; the student will say, "drink."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= label a total of at least 25 functions including at least 4 examples of at least 6 functions, 3=at least 10, 2= at least 5, 1=2 items

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label the class of an individual item.
tasks.question: Can the student identify the class to which an item belongs?
tasks.examples: When shown a picture of a shirt and asked "what is a shirt?, the student will say, "clothes."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=5 items from 10 categories, 3= 3 items from 5 categories, 2= 2 items from 5 categories, 1=2 items from 2 categories

tasks.taskName: Discrimination of question to label aspects of items
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to discriminate whether he is being asked to label the name, function, color, or ownership of an item.
tasks.question: When shown an item, can the student respond to specific questions that are asked in any order about the item including the name, function, color or ownership of the item?
tasks.examples: When shown a red ball, the student must answer "throw it" when asked what do you do with this?, "Tyler's" when asked who it belongs to, "red" when asked what color?, and answer "ball" when asked What is it? Not merely answer "throw ball," red ball," " Tyler's ball," nor "throw Tyler's red ball."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can label at least 3 aspects of an item when asked a specific question about the item 1= can label at least 2 aspects (name, function, color, ownership) of an item when asked a specific question about the item

tasks.taskName: Labels the class of a set of items
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to look at a picture or set of actual items and be able to label the class of the set of items.
tasks.question: Can the student look at a picture or set of actual items and label the class of the set of items ( e.g., food, clothing, animals)?
tasks.examples: When shown a necklace, ring, and earring, the student will say "jewelry"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=5 items from 10 categories, 3= 3 items from 5 categories, 2= 2 items from 5 categories, 1=2 items from 2 categories

tasks.taskName: Labels features of items which are missing or incorrect
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label parts of items of a given picture which are either missing or obviously incorrect (e.g., a car without wheels).
tasks.question: Is the student able to label parts of items of a given picture which are either missing or obviously incorrect?
tasks.examples: When asked "What's wrong?" the student identifies that a snake has "rabbit ears"; and when asked "What is missing?" he identifies that an elephant is missing his ears.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= identifies at least 5 examples in which parts of items of a picture which are missing and 5 examples in which parts are obviously incorrect, 1= can identify at least 5 parts of items of a picture which are either missing or obviously incorrect

tasks.taskObjective: When presented with a set of items in which all except one of the items belongs to a specified category of items (can be based on functions, features or class), the student will be able to name the item which does not belong with that particular set of items.
tasks.question: Can the student identify that a particular item does not belong with a certain set of items?
tasks.examples: For example: given 4 food items and a car, when asked "What does not belong?"; the student will say, "car" When looking at a book with pictures of many items and is asked to label something that is "not an animal" the student says "car" (with a car picture present)
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 3 examples from 10 categories (can be related to functions, features, or classes of items) 3= 3 examples from at least 5 categories, 2= 3 examples from at least 3 categories, 1=3 examples from at least 2 categories (can be related to functions, features, or classes of items)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to identify an obvious problem or emergency.
tasks.question: When shown a picture of an obvious problem situation and asked "What's wrong?" can the student identify the problem?
tasks.examples: A house is on fire, an auto accident, flooding, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can identify at least 3 different obvious problem situations, 1= can identify at least 1 obvious problem situation

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label pictures of common community helpers in his environment.
tasks.question: If you ask "Who is this?" with the picture present, will the student identify common community helpers in his environment?
tasks.examples: Teacher, police, fire fighter, physician, clerk
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 4 or more labels, 3= 3 labels, 2=2 labels, 1=1 label

tasks.taskName: Labels items at a distance when others point to it
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label significant objects located at a distance when others point to the item.
tasks.question: If you point to significant objects in the distance can the student label the items?
tasks.examples: You point to an airplane in the sky and say "look what I see," student says "airplane", label clouds, the moon, etc., a fire truck, a frequently- visited, fast-food restaurant
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can label most significant objects that are more than 100 feet away, 1= can label many significant objects that are at least 10 feet away

tasks.taskObjective: The student will label common sounds in his environment.
tasks.question: When listening to a tape recording of common sounds, or upon hearing a natural environmental sound and asked "What do you hear?", will the student identify the common sound?
tasks.examples: Tools/machinery; saw, drill.....Alert sounds; car horns, train whistles, ambulance/police sirens....animals; events/activities; birthday party, baseball game; vehicles; car, train, airplanes
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 8 sounds, 3= at least 6 sounds, 2= at least 4 sounds, 1= at least 2 sounds

tasks.taskName: Uses carrier phrase when labeling nouns with verbs or adjectives.
tasks.taskObjective: The student will use a carrier phrase when labeling combinations of nouns with verbs or adjectives and will frequently use those carrier phrases without prompting.
tasks.question: If you ask "What is that?" with the item present, will the student identify the item accompanied by a verb or an adjective and include a carrier phrase such as "Thatis a..." ?
tasks.examples: When presented with a ball the student will say "That's a red ball," "Il see a bouncing ball," "There is a big ball," "It's an old ball," "Look, a little ball."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= when spontaneously labeling items, the student will include a carrier phrase at least half of all spontaneous labels and uses at least 2 different carrier phrases, 1= when prompted, the student can label items using at least 2 different phrases

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label the position of an item in relation to other items.
tasks.question: Does the student expressively use prepositions?
tasks.examples: When shown a ball in a cup and asked "Where is the ball?" the student will say "in the cup"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 prepositions, 3= at least 6, 2= at least 4, 1=2 prepositions

tasks.taskName: Uses carrier phrases when using prepositions
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use a carrier phrase when using prepositions and will frequently use those carrier phrases without prompting.
tasks.question: If you ask the student, for example, "Where is the cup?" will he respond using a carrier phrase (e.g., "It's on the table")?
tasks.examples: When asked "Where is the cup?" the student will respond "It's on the table."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= the student will include a carrier phrase at least half of all spontaneous labels using prepositions and uses at least 2 different carrier phrases, 1= when prompted, student can use at least 2 different phrases to label the position of items

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label pronouns.
tasks.question: Does the student use pronouns (he, she, mine, yours, etc.)?
tasks.examples: When asked "Who is jumping?" the student will say "you."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 8 pronouns, 3= at least 5 pronouns, 2= at least 3 pronouns, 1= at least 1 pronoun.

tasks.taskName: Uses carrier phrases when using pronouns
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use a carrier phrase when using pronouns and will frequently use those carrier phrases without prompting.
tasks.question: If you ask the student, for example, "Whose shoe is that?" will he respond using a carrier phrase (e.g., "lt is mine," "That is my shoe")?
tasks.examples: When asked "Who is jumping?" the student will respond "You are jumping."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= the student will include a carrier phrase at least half of all spontaneous labels using pronouns and uses at least 2 different carrier phrases, 1= when prompted, student can use at least 2 different phrases to label items using pronouns

tasks.taskName: Labels and describes events or items presented in a scene
tasks.taskObjective: When shown a picture of a scene or an activity and asked to "tell me about this picture"; the student will be able to label and describe the event, items, and activities presented in the scene.
tasks.question: Can the student label and describe the ongoing events or activities when shown a picture of a scene or an activity and asked to "Tell me about this picture"?
tasks.examples: When shown a scene of a house on fire, the student will say "Fire in a house, fire truck, pulling the fire hose, spraying water on the house." "Eating dinner," "Having a party," "It's a picnic"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= labels at least 4 aspects of a picture including at least one depicted action or the label for the total scene, 1= can label at least one depicted action or the label for the total scene

tasks.taskObjective: When provided with information regarding a certain part of a scene, the student will be able to label specified parts of pictures.
tasks.question: If the student is given information regarding a part of a scene, can the student label specified parts of the picture?
tasks.examples: When shown a picture of a forest and asked "What animal is sitting on the branch?" the student will say "the owl!"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can label items given their classification and another descriptor (action performing, location, size, color, etc.), 1= can label items given either their classification or another descriptor (action performing, location, size, color, etc.)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will label a variety of adverbs.
tasks.question: Does the student use adverbs?
tasks.examples: While observing a turtle walking and the student is asked "How is the turtle moving?" the student says "slowly."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 10 adverbs, 3= at least 6, 2= at least 4, 1= 2 adverbs

tasks.taskObjective: Student will be able to label ongoing facial and behavioral examples of emotions and pictures of faces depicting various emotions.
tasks.question: Can the student label ongoing facial and behavioral examples of emotions and pictures of faces depicting various emotions?
tasks.examples: When observing another child who is crying because his balloon popped and the student is asked how the child feels, the student will say "sad."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 4 emotions (actual examples and pictures), 3= at least 3 emotions (actual examples or pictures), 2= at least 2 emotions, 1= at least 1 emotion (actual example or picture)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label internal events and emotions which are not directly observable by others.
tasks.question: Can the student identify events that can only be perceived by them (e.g., wet pants, stomach ache)?
tasks.examples: Pain, small injuries, itches, happy, sad, surprised, frightened, mad, scared, worried, tired, sleepy, calm, lonely, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can label his own bodily conditions, emotional conditions, visual/auditory/touch/taste stimuli not perceived by others, 3= 3 of the above, 2= 2 of the above, 1= any one of the above

tasks.taskObjective: The student will emit labels containing at least three separate components.
tasks.question: If you ask the student to tell you what he sees, will he label at least three aspects of the stimulus array (e.g., "a big red truck going fast")?
tasks.examples: When shown a picture and asked "What do you see?" the student will say "Daddy's red truck"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 6 words with 4 different parts of speech, 3= at least 5 words with 3 different parts, 2= at least 4 words with 3 different parts, 1= at least 3 words with 3 different parts (noun, verb, adjective, pronoun, adverb, article)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use a variety of carrier phrases when using labels containing at least three separate components and will frequently use those carrier phrases without prompting.
tasks.question: Does the student use a variety of carrier phrases when using labels containing at least three separate components; and if so, does the student frequently use those carrier phrases without prompting?
tasks.examples: When shown a picture and asked "What do you see?" the student will say "l see a big truck going fast"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= when spontaneously labeling items, the student will include a carrier phrase at least half of all spontaneous labels and uses at least 2 different carrier phrases, 1= when prompted, the student can label items using at least 2 different phrases

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to label the nature of ongoing social interactions (e.g., playing, arguing).
tasks.question: Can the student identify the nature of ongoing social interactions?
tasks.examples: "She's embarrassed," arguing, fighting, talking, teasing, playing, working, practicing, busy, upset, friendly, stressed, funny.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=10 labels, 3= 6 labels, 2= 4 labels, 1= 2 labels

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously label items and events throughout the day.
tasks.question: Does the student label items or actions during the day without being asked to label those items and actions?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously labels items or actions at least 20 times per day, 1= spontaneously labels items or actions at least 10 times per day

tasks.taskObjective: While others are singing a song, the student will be able to fill in some words and phrases of songs.
tasks.question: Can the student fill in some words or phrases of songs while others are singing?
tasks.examples: The itsy, bitsy spider...
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 3 phrases from 6 songs, 3= 3 words from 3 songs, 2=2 words from 2 songs, 1=a word from 2 songs

tasks.taskName: Fill in blanks regarding fun items and activities
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to complete an open-ended phrase by supplying the missing word(s) regarding fun items and activities.
tasks.question: If you say a partial phrase regarding fun items and activities will the student supply the missing word(s) (e.g., Winnie the ____)?
tasks.examples: "Let's go up and (down)," "Winnie the
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=10 or more fill-in responses, 3= 5 fill-in responses, 2= 2 fill-in responses, 1= 1 fill-in response

tasks.taskName: Sign English words (for students who use ASL)
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to provide a sign (American Sign Language (ASL) when given an English word.
tasks.question: Can the student show you ASL signs when given only spoken words?
tasks.examples: When a person says "Sign apple," the student will make the American Sign Language sign for "apple."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 25 signs, 3= 15 signs, 2=5 signs, 1=2 signs (Note: score = Not Applicable (NA) if the student can say more than 50 words and/or does not use ASL signs)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to provide the name of the animal when given the animal sound or vice versa.
tasks.question: Can the student provide the corresponding name of the animal given a sound, or vice versa?
tasks.examples: When the student hears the statement "A dog says....," the student will say "woof, woof"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= makes 8 animal sounds given names of animal and names 8 animals when given the sound made by the animal, 3= 6 sounds or names, 2= 4 sounds or names, 1=2 sounds or names

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to provide answers to questions regarding personal information.
tasks.question: Can the student provide information about himself?
tasks.examples: When asked "What's your name?" the student will state his name.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 4 pieces of information about self (e.g., name, age, phone, siblings, parents' names, etc.), 3= 3 pieces of information, 2= 2 pieces of information, 1= 1 piece of information about self

tasks.taskName: Fill in words describing common activities
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to fill in the remaining word of a phrase describing an ongoing activity.
tasks.question: Can the student fill in the remaining word of a phrase in the context of an ongoing activity (e.g., It's time to wash your _)?
tasks.examples: As you lead the child to the sink and you say "It's time to wash your ____" the student will say "hands"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=10 or more fill-in responses, 3= 5 fill-in responses, 2= 2 fill-in responses,1= 1 fill-in response

tasks.taskObjective: When asked "What goes with (____)?," the student will be able to say some items which is associated (related) with the stated item (e.g., says "bed" when hears "What goes with a pillow?).
tasks.question: Can the student name objects which are commonly associated (related) with an item that you mention?
tasks.examples: "What goes with ...s0cks?" "shoes," "...bat"- "ball," "...cup"- "juice," "...pillow"- "bed"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can say at least 2 related items for 20 or more named items, 3= 2 related items for each of 10 named items, 2= 1 related item for 10 items, 1= can say at least 1 related item for each of 5 named items

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to fill in the remaining word naming the item in a phrase related to the function of an item.
tasks.question: Can the student fill in the remaining word of a phrase related to a function of an item (e.g., You cut paper with scissors )?
tasks.examples: When the student hears the statement "You ride in a..." the student says "car."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more fill-ins with two responses, 3= 10 fill-ins with two responses, 2= 5 fill-in responses, 1= 2 fill-in responses
tasks.protocolNotes: See Appendix 14: Intraverbal Fill-in List Note that intraverbal skills usually start to develop in the context of activities and later occur in the absence of the items that were involved in those activities.

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to fill in the remaining word in a phrase naming the function of an item.
tasks.question: Can the student fill in the remaining word of a phrase related to a function of an item (e.g., You use scissors to _cut_)?
tasks.examples: You use scissors to .... cut, you use a spoon to ...... cat
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more fill-ins with two responses, 3= 10 fill-ins with two responses, 2= 5 fill-in responses, 1= 2 fill-in responses

tasks.taskName: Answers "What" questions regarding items found in home
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer "What" questions regarding items found in home.
tasks.question: Does the student answer "What" questions regarding items found in home?
tasks.examples: When the student is asked "What can you find in the bathroom?" the student says "toilet, bathtub, towels," "What can you find in the refrigerator?" the student says "milk, eggs, juice"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= answers 30 or more questions including at least 3 responses for at least 5 locations (e.g., bedroom, refrigerator, kitchen, closet, living room), 3= 15 questions, 2= 10 questions, 1= answers at least 5 questions

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer "What" questions regarding the function of items.
tasks.question: Does the student answer "What" questions regarding the functions of items?
tasks.examples: When the student is asked "What can you use to cut paper?", the student says "scissors," "What can you use to write?" the student says "pen"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= answers 50 or more questions, 3= 25 questions, 2= 10 questions, 1= answers at least 5 questions

tasks.taskName: Answers "Where" questions regarding items found in home or classroom
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer "Where" questions regarding items found in home or classroom.
tasks.question: Does the student answer "Where" questions regarding items found in home or classroom?
tasks.examples: When the student is asked "Where do you find milk?", the student says "refrigerator," When the student is asked "Where do you find a toilet?" the student says "bathroom"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= answers 30 or more questions, 3= 15 questions, 2= 10 questions, 1= answers at least 5 questions

tasks.taskName: Answers "Where" questions regarding activities done at home or school
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer "Where" questions regarding activities done at home or school.
tasks.question: Does the student answer "Where" questions regarding activities done at home or school?
tasks.examples: When the student is asked "Where do you sleep?" the student says "bedroom," When the student is asked "Where do you put your dirty clothes?" the student says "hamper"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= answers 30 or more questions, 3= 15 questions, 2= 10 questions, 1= answers at least 5 questions

tasks.taskName: Fill in item given the class
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to fill in the remaining word of a phrase to name an item/example of a specified class of items.
tasks.question: Can the student fill in the remaining word of a phrase to name an item/example of a specified class of items?
tasks.examples: Atype of animal is a ... "dog" "cat", Atype of food is a... "hamburger"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more fill-ins with two responses, 3= 10 fill-ins with two responses, 2= 5 fill-in responses, 1= 2 fill-in responses

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to verbally provide members of specific categories.
tasks.question: Can the student provide members of a specified category?
tasks.examples: When asked to "name some animals" the student says "horse, dog, cow" Things to eat "apples, cereal, hamburger, pizza"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 categories with 4 responses, 3= 10 categories with 3 responses, 2= 5 categories with 2 responses, 1= 2 categories with 2 responses.

tasks.taskName: Fill in features given the item
tasks.taskObjective: When told the name of the item, the student will be able to fill in the remaining word in a phrase naming a feature of the item.
tasks.question: When told the name of the item, can the student fill in the remaining word of a phrase to name a feature of the item (e.g., a dog has a tail )?
tasks.examples: Acar has a ... "wheel" "horn" "door"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more fill-ins with two responses, 3= 10 fill-ins with two responses, 2= 5 fill-in responses, 1= 2 fill-in responses

tasks.taskName: Fill in item given its feature
tasks.taskObjective: When told a feature of an item, the student will be able to fill in the remaining word in a phrase to name the item.
tasks.question: When told a feature of an item, can the student fill in the remaining word of a phrase to name the item (e.g., something that has wheels is a car)?
tasks.examples: Something that has a tail ... dog, something with wheels, it's a ..... car
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more fill-ins with two responses, 3= 10 fill-ins with two responses, 2= 5 fill-in responses, 1= 2 fill-in responses

tasks.taskName: Fill in class given the item
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to fill in the remaining word of a phrase to specify the class of a given item/example.
tasks.question: Can the student fill in the remaining word of a phrase to specify the class of a given item/example (e.g., a dog is an _animal )?
tasks.examples: Apples are a type of ..... "Food", acatis an ...... "Animal".
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more fill-ins with two responses, 3= 10 fill-ins with two responses, 2= 5 fill-in responses, 1= 2 fill-in responses

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to name items which had previously been observed.
tasks.question: Can the student name items or activities which had previously been observed?
tasks.examples: Go outside to see a fire truck, come back into classroom and name what he had observed when outside.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= states 2 or more items one hour after the observation, 3= 1 item after 10 minutes, 2= 1 item after 5 minutes, 1= 1 item immediately after the observation

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to name an activity that he has recently observed.
tasks.question: Can the student name the activity that he has recently observed?
tasks.examples: Go outside and observes people playing baseball, come back into classroom and name the activity he observed when outside. Sees brother reading a book in living room, goes into kitchen and states his brother's activity
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= states the activity one hour after seeing the activity, 3= states activity after 10 minutes, 2= states activity after 5 minutes, 1= states activity immediately after the observing the activity

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to name people who had previously been observed.
tasks.question: Can the student name people who had previously been observed?
tasks.examples: Go outside and play with students in a sandbox, come back into classroom and name the people who were in the sandbox.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= states 2 or more people one hour after the observation, 3= 1 person after 10 minutes, 2= 1 person after 5 minutes, 1= 1 person immediately after the observation

tasks.taskName: With visual display, makes related statements (not naming)
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to make a variety of related comments (not including naming of items) regarding pictures of items or activities.
tasks.question: When shown a picture and told something about the picture "They're having a picnic," does the student make comments regarding items or activities related to what is observed in the picture?
tasks.examples: When shown a picture of people at a picnic with a grill (but can't see the food) and the student is told "They're having a picnic," the child makes comments such as "They're cooking hot dogs and hamburgers" or "Don't touch, it's hot."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= expands/comments on 20 pictures, 3= expands/ comments on 10 pictures, 2= expands/comments on 5 pictures, 1= expands/ comments on 1 picture

tasks.taskName: Answers "What" questions relevant to items found in the community
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to give single response answers regarding questions concerning what he might see in various locations in his community.
tasks.question: Can the student answer questions regarding what he might see in various locations in his community?
tasks.examples: When asked "What do you see at the park?" the student says "swings"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more questions answered, 3= 10 questions answered, 2= 5 questions answered, 1= 2 questions answered

tasks.taskName: Answers "What" questions relevant to activities that he can doin the community
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to give single response answers regarding questions concerning what he could do in various locations in his community.
tasks.question: Can the student answer questions regarding what he could do in various locations in his community?
tasks.examples: When asked "What can you do at the grocery store?" the student says "buy cookies," "What can you do at the park?" the student says "go down the slide"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more questions answered, 3= 10 questions answered, 2= 5 questions answered, 1= 2 questions answered

tasks.taskName: Answers "Where" questions regarding activities and items found in the community
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer "Where" questions regarding activities and items found in the community.
tasks.question: Does the student answer "Where" questions regarding activities and items found in the community?
tasks.examples: When the student is asked "where can we buy milk?" the student says "grocery store," When the student is asked "Where do you play in the sandbox?" the student says "school"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= answers 30 or more questions, 3= 15 questions, 2= 10 questions, 1= answers at least 5 questions

tasks.taskName: Answers questions with multiple responses concerning his immediate community
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to provide several answers to questions concerning his immediate community.
tasks.question: Can the student answer questions which require multiple responses related to services in his community (e.g., What can you get at a grocery store)?
tasks.examples: When asked "Tell me as many things as you can that you can get from a grocery store" the student says "bananas, corn, meat, milk, bread"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 categories with 3 responses, 3= 10 categories with 3 responses, 2= 5 categories with 2 responses, 1= 2 categories with 2 responses

tasks.taskName: States class given multiple class members (examples)
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to identify the class when told two or more items from the class.
tasks.question: Can the student identify the class when told two or more items from the class?
tasks.examples: When told "apple, banana, and pear are all ..."; the student says "fruit," "food," or "things you eat"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 classes when told 2 or more members, 3= 10 classes, 2= 5 classes, 1= class when told 2 or more members.

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer "Who/Whose" questions.
tasks.question: Does the student answer "Who/Whose" questions?
tasks.examples: "Whose car did you ride in today?" (Daddy's), "Who likes to eat pizza? (Mom)," "Who do you see when you're sick?," "Who puts out fires?"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= answers 50 or more questions, 3= 25 questions, 2= 10 questions, 1= answers at least 5 questions

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer "When" questions.
tasks.question: Does the student answer "When" questions?
tasks.examples: "When do you sleep?" "When do you eat?"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= answers 50 or more questions, 3= 25 questions, 2= 10 questions,1= answers at least 5 questions

tasks.taskName: Discrimination of questions asked about items and activities
tasks.taskObjective: When discussing an item or activity, the student will be able to discriminate whether he is being asked a "What" "Where," "Who," or "When" question.
tasks.question: Can the student answer "What" "Where," "Who," and "When" questions when they are asked in any order?
tasks.examples: Where do you go to buy milk?, Who takes you to the store? What can you get to eat at the store? When do you go to the store? What color is an apple? Where do we get apples? What do we do with apples?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can answer at least four types of questions in any order 1=can answer at least two types of questions in any order

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer "Which" questions.
tasks.question: Does the student answer "Which" questions?
tasks.examples: "Which one is an animal, a dog or a shoe?"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= answers 50 or more questions, 3= 25 questions, 2= 10 questions,1= answers at least 5 questions

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer "How" questions.
tasks.question: Does the student answer "How" questions?
tasks.examples: "How do you get to school?"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= answers 50 or more questions, 3= 25 questions, 2= 10 questions, 1= answers at least 5 questions

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer "Why" questions.
tasks.question: Does the student answer "Why" questions?
tasks.examples: Why do you wash your hands?, Why do you sleep?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= answers 50 or more questions, 3= 25 questions, 2= 10 questions, 1= answers at least 5 questions

tasks.taskName: Describes steps in sequence of a daily activity
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to state the steps in sequence of a daily activity.
tasks.question: Can the student state the steps in sequence of a daily activity?
tasks.examples: When asked "How do you wash your hands?" the student will say "go to the sink, turn on the water, rub hands with soap....."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 5 or more steps in at least 2 sequences, 3= 4 stepsina sequence, 2=3 stepsin a sequence, 1=2 stepsin a sequence

tasks.taskName: States activity when told sequence of actions
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to state the activity being described when told a sequence of actions.
tasks.question: Can the student state the activity being described when told a sequence of actions?
tasks.examples: When asked "What am I doing?" and given the description, "I go to the sink, turn on the water, wet my hands, pick-up the soap...," the student will say "washing hands."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more questions answered, 3= 10 questions answered, 2= 5 questions answered, 1= 2 questions answered

tasks.taskName: States item when told its functions, features, or class (multiple features)
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to give the name of an item after being provided with multiple aspects of the item (e.g., its functions, features, class).
tasks.question: Can the student give the name of an item after being told multiple aspects of the item (e.g., its functions, features, class)?
tasks.examples: Given the description, "It's crunchy, you eat it, it's salty, it comes in a bag...," the student will say "potato chip."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more questions answered, 3= 10 questions answered, 2= 5 questions answered, 1= 2 questions answered

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to move his head or say "Yes" or "No" to answer questions about an item or activity which is not present.
tasks.question: Can the student say "yes" or "no" or move his head to answer questions about non- present items or events (e.g., can dogs fly?)?
tasks.examples: When the student is asked "Can I buy gas at a shoe store?" the student says "no"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can answer at least 50 questions, 3= at least 25 questions, 2= at least 10 questions, 1= at least 5 questions about items not present

tasks.taskName: Answers questions containing two critical stimuli (multiple component questions with multiple responses)
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to provide multiple answers to questions which contains two critical stimuli.
tasks.question: Can the student answer questions which require him to identify several items which meet at least two specified criteria (e.g., some farm animals)?
tasks.examples: When the student is asked to name some "hot foods" the student says "pizza, spaghetti..."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 4 responses provided to 5 different questions, 3= 3 responses provided to 4 different questions, 2= 2 responses provided for 3 questions, 1=2 responses provided for 1 question

tasks.taskName: Answers questions containing three critical stimuli (multiple component questions with multiple responses)
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to provide multiple answers to questions which contain three critical stimuli.
tasks.question: Can the student answer questions which require him to identify several items which meet at least three specified criteria (e.g., big animals at the 200)?
tasks.examples: When the student is asked to name some "big farm animals" the student says "horse, and cow"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 4 responses provided to 5 different questions, 3=3 responses provided to 4 different questions, 2= 2 responses provided for 3 questions, 1=2 responses provided for 1 question

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to describe items by identifying what you do with the item, some of its features and/or its classification.
tasks.question: Can the student describe items by identifying what you do with the item, some of its features and classification?
tasks.examples: When asked to describe a car, the student is able to say that you ride in it to go places, it has wheels and you park it in a garage. Cereal is something you eat for breakfast, put in a bowl and pour milk on it.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can describe at least 20 items stating at least 3 relevant details about the items (not including the label/name of the items) 1=can describe at least 10 items stating at least 2 relevant details about the items (not including the label/name of the items)

tasks.taskName: Describes steps before and after in sequence of a daily activity
