tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to state the steps which occur before and after a given step in sequence of a daily activity.
tasks.question: Can the student state the steps which occur before and after a given step in sequence of a daily activity?
tasks.examples: When asked what you do before you eat lunch, student indicates "wash hands." When asked what you do after lunch, student indicates "throw trash away."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can state steps both before and after for 10 different activities, 3= can state steps both before and after for 5 activities, 2= can state 1 step either before or after for 2 activities, 1= can state 1 step either before or a single activity

tasks.taskName: Answers questions concerning past and upcoming events
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer questions which require a single response concerning his past and upcoming events.
tasks.question: Can the student answer questions which require a single response concerning his past and upcoming events?
tasks.examples: Upon arrival at school ... Can you tell me what you had for breakfast? Can you tell me what you are going to do this weekend?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 4 answers regarding past and future events over a month away, 3= 2 answers regarding past or future events over a month away, 2= 2 answers regarding past or future events within a week, 1= at least 2 answers regarding past or future events of that day

tasks.taskName: Maintains a conversation with an adult or peer
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to maintain a conversation on a single topic for at least five verbal exchanges.
tasks.question: Can the student engage in conversations?
tasks.examples: Five exchanges between the student and another about a baseball game
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= five exchanges on at least 10 different topics including the student asking at least one novel question or making at least one novel comment, 1=3 exchanges on at least 5 different topics

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer questions asked in a different way than was originally taught.
tasks.question: Can the student answer questions asked in a slightly different way than was originally taught?
tasks.examples: When originally taught to answer the question "What do you do with a car?" (go for rides) the student can also answer similar questions such as "Can you tell me what a car does?" or" What's a car for?"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more novel questions answered, 3= 10 novel questions answered, 2= 5 novel questions answered, 1= 2 novel questions answered

tasks.taskName: Answers questions relevant to current events
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to answer questions concerning current events.
tasks.question: Can the student provide single answers to questions related to events in his community?
tasks.examples: When asked "Can you tell me what you're going to do for the Fourth of July?" the student says "see fireworks"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 or more questions answered, 3= 10 questions answered, 2= 5 questions answered, 1= 2 questions answered

tasks.taskName: Answers questions with multiple responses concerning current events
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to provide several answers to questions concerning current events.
tasks.question: Can the student provide multiple answers to questions related to events in his community (e.g., What can you do at the park)?
tasks.examples: When asked "Can you tell me as many things as you can that you can that you do on the Fourth of July?" the student says "see fireworks, see a parade, have a barbecue"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 categories with 3 responses, 3= 10 categories with 3 responses, 2= 5 categories with 2 responses, 1= 2 categories with 1 or 2 responses

tasks.taskName: Answers questions with multiple responses in group discussions
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to provide several answers to questions regarding a variety of topics in a group discussion.
tasks.question: Can the student provide multiple answers to questions regarding a variety of topics in a group (e.g., morning circle) discussion (e.g., What happened on the way into the classroom that morning)?
tasks.examples: When asked "What happened this morning when we were coming inside?" the student says "It was raining, Jason stepped in a puddle, his shoes got wet." When asked "What did we do yesterday?" the student says " made cookies and went to park."
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= provides at least 2 comments for at least 3 topics in a 20 minute discussion, 1= provides at least 1 comment for at least 2 topics in a 10 minute discussion

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to tell a story or describe an event concerning a single topic relating at least five separate components.
tasks.question: Can the student tell a story or describe an event concerning a single topic (e.g., his last trip to the park)?
tasks.examples: Student can describe his last trip to the zoo or park (what he did, who was there, what he saw, etc.), Student can tell a story about The Three Little Pigs, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= at least five descriptions of events or stories that contains at least 5 components, 1= at least one description an event or story that contains at least 3 components

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously add or make appropriate related comments during an ongoing conversation or discussion.
tasks.question: Does the student spontaneously add or make appropriate related comments during an ongoing conversation or discussion?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously adds or makes related comments during an ongoing conversation or discussion at least 10 times per day, 1= spontaneously adds or makes related comments during an ongoing conversation or discussion at least 10 times per week (unprompted)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will make a variety of spontaneous vocalizations which include speech sounds.
tasks.question: Does the student say words or make some sounds heard in speech?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= student frequently says words or makes speech sounds totaling at least 10 minutes per hour, 3= total 5 minutes per hour, 2= total 2 minutes per hour, 1= makes speech sounds totaling at least 10 minutes per day

tasks.taskName: Spontaneously says words or approximations to words
tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously say a variety of words or approximations to words.
tasks.question: Does the student spontaneously say words or approximations to words?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= spontaneously says an average of at least 30 words per hour (including at least 5 different words), 3= average of at least 10 words per hour, 2= an average of at least 1 word per hour, 1= spontaneously says an average of at least 5 words per day

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously say a variety of phrases.
tasks.question: Does the student spontaneously say phrases?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= spontaneously says an average of at least 30 phrases per day (including at least 5 different words), 3= average of 10 phrases per day, 2= an average of at least 5 phrases per day, 1= spontaneously says an average of at least 1 phrase per day

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously sing songs while others are singing, while watching videos or listening to other sources.
tasks.question: Does the student sing songs along with others singing a song?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= sings at least 2 phrases from each of 5 songs, 3= sings 1 phrase from each of 5 songs, 2= sings 1 phrase from 2 songs, 1= sings 1 word from 1 song

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously sing songs without models.
tasks.question: Does the student sing songs without hearing songs?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= sings at least 2 phrases from each of 5 songs, 3= sings 1 phrase from each of 5 songs, 2= sings 1 phrase from 2 songs, 1= sings 1 word from 1 song

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously repeat words said by others.
tasks.question: Does the student spontaneously repeat words said by others?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously repeats words said by others at least 5 times per day, 1= spontaneously repeats words said by others at least 5 times per week

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously request items, actions or activities.
tasks.question: Does the student spontaneously request items, actions or activities?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously requests at least 10 items or actions per day, 1= spontaneously requests at least 10 items or actions per week

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously label items, actions, or events.
tasks.question: Does the student spontaneously label items, actions, or events?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously labels items, actions, or events at least 10 times per day, 1= spontaneously labels items, actions, or events at least 10 times per week

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously add or make appropriate related comments during an ongoing conversation or discussion.
tasks.question: Does the student spontaneously add or make appropriate related comments during an ongoing conversation or discussion?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously adds or makes related comments during an ongoing conversation or discussion at least 10 times per day, 1= spontaneously adds or makes related comments during an ongoing conversation or discussion at least 10 times per week

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to speak in phrases or sentences of up to at least five words.
tasks.question: What is the average number of words in a phrase or sentence that the student says when talking?
tasks.examples: The boy is going home.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4 = 5 or more word phrases or sentences, 3 =4 word phrases or sentences, 2 = 3 word phrases or sentences, 1 = 2 word phrases or sentences

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to combine words in phrases or sentences using correct word order (e.g., adverb + noun, adjective + noun, noun + verb).
tasks.question: Does the student use correct word order when speaking in phrases or sentences (e.g., adverb + noun, adjective + noun, noun + verb)?
tasks.examples: adjective + noun: bouncing ball, barking dog; noun + verb: boy is running; articles: The boy is running
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4 = 4 or more word sentences usually in correct order, 3 = sometimes 4 word sentences in correct order, 2 = sometimes 3 word sentences in correct order, 1 = sometimes 2 word phrases in correct order

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to include articles (e.g., a, an, the) when speaking in phrases or sentences.
tasks.question: Does the student include articles (e.g., a, an, the) when speaking in phrases or sentences?
tasks.examples: A dog, an apple, the pig
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= uses articles most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally uses articles when appropriate

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to indicate regular present tense by adding "ing" to the end of verbs (e.g., running, jumping).
tasks.question: Does the student indicate present tense by adding "ing" to the end of verbs (e.g., running, jumping)?
tasks.examples: eating, sleeping, washing, running, jumping
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= adds "ing" to the end of verbs most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally adds "ing" to the end of verbs when appropriate

tasks.taskObjective: The student will add an "s" (or "es") sound at the end of words to indicate plurals (e.g., shoes, glasses).
tasks.question: Does the student add 's' or 'es' to the end of words to indicate plurals (e.g., shoes, glasses)?
tasks.examples: hats, shoes, cups, dogs, cats, glasses
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= adds "s" to the end of words most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally adds "s" to the end of words when appropriate

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to indicate past tense by changing the form of verbs (e.g., swim-swam, run-ran, sing-sang, fall-fell, sleep-slept, break-broke, keep-kept).
tasks.question: Is the student able to change the form of verbs to indicate past tense (e.g., swim-swam, run- ran, sing-sang, fall-fell, sleep-slept, break-broke, keep-kept)?
tasks.examples: swim-swam, run-ran, sing-sang, fall-fell, sleep- slept, break-broke, keep- kept
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= uses correct irregular past tense most of the time, 1= occasionally uses correct irregular past tense

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use contractions (e.g., can't, won't, didn't) when speaking in phrases or sentences.
tasks.question: Does the student use contractions (e.g., cant, won't, didn't) when speaking in phrases or sentences?
tasks.examples: can't, won', didn't, couldn't, they're, we've, I've
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= uses contractions most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally uses contractions when appropriate

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to indicate present tense by combining "am" and "is" with verbs (e.g., am writing, is jumping) when speaking in phrases or sentences.
tasks.question: Does the student indicate present tense by combining "am" and "is" with verbs (e.g., am writing, is jumping) when speaking in phrases or sentences?
tasks.examples: boy is running, I'm hungry, he's eating, I'm coloring, | am jumping
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2=uses "am" or "is" with verbs to indicate present tense most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally uses "am" or "is" with verbs to indicate present tense when appropriate

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to indicate regular past tense by adding "d," or "ed" (e.g, hiked, jumped).
tasks.question: Does the student add "d, "or "ed" to the end of words to indicate past tense (e.g., hiked, jumped)?
tasks.examples: hiked, jumped
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= adds "d," or "ed" to verbs to indicate regular past tense most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally adds "d," or "ed" to verbs to indicate regular past tense when appropriate

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to indicate possession by adding "s" to nouns and pronouns (e.g., yours, theirs, daddy's hat).
tasks.question: Does the student add "s" to nouns and pronouns to indicate possession (e.g., daddy's hat, the cat's tail)?
tasks.examples: Daddy's car, the cat's tail
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= adds "s" to nouns or pronouns to indicate possession most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally adds "s" to nouns or pronouns to indicate possession when appropriate

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to indicate negation (e.g., didn't, won't, doesn't, isn't, not, no more, all gone) when speaking in phrases or sentences.
tasks.question: Does the student indicate negation (e.g., didn't, won't, doesn't, isn't, not, no more, all gone) when speaking in phrases or sentences?
tasks.examples: didn't, won't, doesn't, isn't, can't, not, no more, all gone
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= indicates negation most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally indicates negation when appropriate

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to indicate location (e.g., here, there) when speaking in phrases or sentences.
tasks.question: Does the student indicate location (e.g., here, there) when speaking in phrases or sentences?
tasks.examples: here, there
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= indicates location most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally indicates location when appropriate

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to indicate future tense (e.g., | will go home) when speaking in phrases or sentences.
tasks.question: Does the student indicate future tense (e.g., | will go home) when speaking in phrases or sentences?
tasks.examples: | will go home. | am going to get my book tomorrow. | should do it. | could make it later. | shall look at it later.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= indicates future tense most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally indicates future tense when appropriate

tasks.taskObjective: The student will use conjunctions to combine words and phrases (e.g., and, but, if, given, nor, or, because, then, only).
tasks.question: Does the student use conjunctions to combine words and phrases?
tasks.examples: dog and cat, mom _or_ dad, warm but not hot
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= uses conjunctions most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally uses conjunctions when appropriate

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use irregular plurals (e.g., mouse-mice, foot-feet, goose- geese).
tasks.question: Does the student correctly use irregular plurals (e.g., mouse- mice, foot-feet, goose- geese)?
tasks.examples: mouse-mice, foot-feet, goose-geese
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= uses correct irregular plurals most of the time, 1= occasionally uses correct irregular plurals

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to add suffixes to words to indicate comparisons (e.g., ...er asin bigger, ...est asin biggest).
tasks.question: Does the student add suffixes to words to indicate comparisons (e.g., ...er asin bigger, ...est as in biggest)?
tasks.examples: ...er asin bigger, ...est as in biggest
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= adds "er" or "est" to words to indicate comparison most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally adds "er" or "est" to words to indicate comparison when appropriate

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to indicate specific items (e.g., this, that, these, those) when speaking in phrases or sentences.
tasks.question: Does the student indicate specific items (e.g., this, that, these, those) when speaking in phrases or sentences?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= uses words such as "this," "that," "these," or "those" to specify specific items most of the time, 1= occasionally uses words to specify specific items

tasks.taskName: Label strength of a verbal response
tasks.taskObjective: Student will use words or phrases to describe his certainty of his responses (e.g., I think, ...guess, ... know, ...believe).
tasks.question: Does the student use words or phrases to describe his certainty of a statement?
tasks.examples: I think I finished the drawing. I guess, I know, I believe, perhaps, It seems like...
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= uses words to indicate the certainty of a statement most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally uses words to indicate the certainty of a statement

tasks.taskObjective: Student will use words or phrases to quantify a verbal response (e.g., all, some, sometimes, never, a, the, always).
tasks.question: Does the student use words to quantify a statement?
tasks.examples: | want all the trucks. all, sometimes, never, a, the, always
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= uses words to indicate the quantification in a statement most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally uses words to indicate quantification in a statement

tasks.taskName: Label emotional state associated with a verbal response
tasks.taskObjective: Student will use words or phrases to describe an emotional state related to a statement (e.g., I regret to inform you..., I'm sorry, but... I'm happy to say...).
tasks.question: Does the student use words or phrases to describe an emotional state related to a statement?
tasks.examples: I'm sorry that you are sick, I'm sad that I can't go, I'm glad you came with me.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= uses words to indicate the emotional state associated with making a statement most of the time when appropriate, 1= occasionally uses words to indicate the emotional state associated with making a statement

tasks.taskObjective: The student will actively explore a variety of toys in the environment.
tasks.question: Does the student actively explore available toys?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= manipulates a toy or toys for at least 2 of a 10 minute period, 1=picks up and/or manipulates at least 1 toy in a ten minute period

tasks.taskName: Allows others to manipulate/ touch toys
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to allow adults and children to be near them while they are playing with toys and allow others to occasionally manipulate the toys during the interaction.
tasks.question: Does the student allow you to be near him when he is playing with toys and allow you to occasionally touch or move the toys he is using?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= allows other students or adults to occasionally manipulate toys that they are using, 1= allows other students to be near them when playing with a toy

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to engage in appropriate independent outdoor activities.
tasks.question: Does the student engage in appropriate independent outdoor play activities ?
tasks.examples: shoot basketball; use slide, swings, wagon, sandbox, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= selects and engages in at least 3 activities for at least 15 minutes, 3= 3 activities for 10 minutes, 2= 2 activities for 10 minutes, 1=2 activities for 5 minutes

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to engage in appropriate independent indoor leisure activities.
tasks.question: Does the student engage in appropriate independent indoor leisure activities?
tasks.examples: look at books or videos, listen to music, complete puzzles
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= selects and engages in at least 3 activities for at least 15 minutes, 3= 3 activities for 10 minutes, 2= 2 activities for 10 minutes, 1=2 activities for 5 minutes

tasks.taskName: Plays with toys/ manipulates toys as designed
tasks.taskObjective: The student will actively play with toys as designed.
tasks.question: Does the student actively play with toys?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= plays with at least two toys as designed without prompts for up to 10 minutes, 1= plays with at least one toy as designed for up to 10 minutes with occasional prompts

tasks.taskName: Independently plays with toys and engages in verbal behavior
tasks.taskObjective: The student will talk while engaging in independent play activities.
tasks.question: Does the student talk while playing by himself?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= while playing independently, engages in at least 10 verbal responses in a 20 minute period, 3=5 verbal responses, 2= 2 verbal responses, 1= 1 verbal response in a 20 minute period

tasks.taskName: Multiple responses with toys related to a theme
tasks.taskObjective: The student will play with toys consistent with an identifiable theme (e.g., cooking implements, dolls, action figures).
tasks.question: Does the student play with toys (multiple responses) consistent with an identifiable theme?
tasks.examples: Moves a toy car down a ramp, pretends to put gas into the car, moves the car into a garage. Pretends to have a tea party.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= spontaneously does at least 5 activities with 5 different toys 3= at least 5 activities for 2 toys 2= at least 5 related activities with one toy, 1= spontaneously does at least 2 related activities with one toy

tasks.taskObjective: The student will engage in interactive play activities with other students.
tasks.question: Does the student play with other children?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= Mutually interacts with other students and toys for up to 10 minutes (requests included), 3= Mutually interacts with other students and toys for up to 5 minutes (requests included), 2= gives other students toys when they request them, and accepts offered toys from other students, 1= accepts offered toys from other students
tasks.protocolNotes: Modified - removed allow others to be near- , allows other students to be near them when playing with a toy

tasks.taskName: Plays interactively with a variety of peers
tasks.taskObjective: The student will engage in interactive play activities with a variety of peers.
tasks.question: Does the student play with several of his peers, either individually or in a group activity?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= interactively plays with at least 8 different peers (individual or group interactions), 3= interactively plays with at least 6 different peers, 2= interactively plays with at least 4 different peers, 1= interactively plays with at least 2 different peers (individual or group interactions)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will act out roles of characters or activities while playing.
tasks.question: Can the student pretend to be somebody or pretend to do an activity (e.g., pretend to be Mommy, Daddy, a dog, a doctor, serving tea, play dress-up)?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can pretend to be at least 10 characters or pretend to do activities, 3= at least 5 characters or activities, 2= at least 2 characters or activities, 1= at least 1 character or activity

tasks.taskName: Plays with toys and talks with peers
tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask for items and actions, label items and actions, and make other related comments while engaging in play activities.
tasks.question: Does the student talk about what he is doing while playing with other children?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=while playing with a peer, engages in at least 10 verbal responses to the peer in a 10 minute period, 3= 5 verbal responses in 10 minutes, 2=, 2 verbal responses in 10 minutes, 1=1 verbal response in a 10 minute period

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to independently play simple games involving rolling, throwing, kicking and bouncing a ball to a peer for at least 5 exchanges.
tasks.question: Can the student independently play games that involve rolling, throwing, kicking, and bouncing a ball to a peer?
tasks.examples: roll, throw, kick a ball to a peer;
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can independently perform at least three ball actions with a peer for up to 5 exchanges (i.e., watches for ball to be thrown, observes partner being ready to recieve), 3= can independently perform 2 ball actions for at least 3 exchanges, 2= can perform 1 action if given only occasional prompts to watch to see if peer is ready OR to attend to peer about to perform the action, 1= can perform 1 action but requires occasional prompts to look to see if peer is ready AND to attend to peer about to perform the action

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to allow peers to guide a coordinated play activity (follow directions from peers).
tasks.question: Does the student allow peers to give him instructions and direct his actions while engaging in interactive activities?
tasks.examples: Roll a ball fast or slow (based on the action of the peer or upon a request from the peer), move a parachute up and down based on an instruction or motor action of a peer, acts as an "assistant" when building a house using blocks, swinging a jump rope' at the same speed as a peer, switch from throwing a ball to bouncing a ball to a peer, waits for signal before moving the train
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= follows both stated and implied directions from peers in at least four play activities, 3= follows both stated and implied directions from peers in at least three play activities, 2= follows both stated and implied directions from peers in at least one play activity, 1= follows stated directions from peers to perform at least one activity without requiring extensive peer prompting

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to play interactive games that require him to attend to the actions of others and adjust his participation based on his peers' behavior.
tasks.question: Can the student play interactive games that require him to attend to the actions of others and adjust his participation based on his peers’ behavior?
tasks.examples: Play "Tag," "You're it"; "Duck, Duck Goose"; relay race; kick baseball
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can play at least 3 interactive games without assistance, 3= can play at least 2 interactive games without assistance, 2= only needs some prompts either to attend to his turn OR to complete the action (not both), 1= can participate in playing games but needs some prompts to attend to when it is his turn and some prompts to complete the necessary actions of the game (not totally prompted)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to play board games with peers.
tasks.question: Can the student play board games with his peers?
tasks.examples: Candyland, Uno, Go Fish, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can play at least three board games without assistance, 3= can play at least two board games without assistance, 2= only needs some prompts either to attend to his turn OR to complete the action (not both), 1= can participate in playing board games but needs some prompts to attend to when it is his turn and some prompts to complete the necessary actions of the game (not totally prompted)

tasks.taskName: Appropriate when near peers or siblings
tasks.taskObjective: The student will engage in appropriate physical interaction behavior while in close physical proximity with peers or siblings.
tasks.question: Is the student able to be physically near other students or siblings without engaging in disruptive behavior?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= student is appropriate when near peers/siblings for at least 30 minutes, 3=appropriate for 15 minutes, 2=student is appropriate for 5 minutes with only 1 verbal prompt, 1=student is appropriate for at least 5 minutes but requires multiple verbal prompts

tasks.taskObjective: When offered a preferred item, the student will take the item from both peers and adults.
tasks.question: When a preferred item is offered to the student, will the student take the item from both peers and adults?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= will usually walk to and take the preferred item from peers and adults who are more than 8 feet away, 1= will take the preferred item from peers and adults who are less than 3 feet away

tasks.taskName: Tolerates/ responds appropriately to positive touches by peers or siblings
tasks.taskObjective: The student will respond appropriately (i.e., not cry or attempt to physically get away from a person) to positive physical interactions initiated by others (e.g., take and hold his hand, "high 5", physically help him get onto a swing).
tasks.question: Does the student respond appropriately to positive physical interactions initiated by others (e.g., take and hold their hand, "high 5", physically help him get onto a swing)?
tasks.examples: take and hold hand, give "high 5", help solve a problem
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily allows both peers/siblings and adults to touch in a positive manner and assist them in most situations, 1= when carefully approached allows some individuals to touch in a positive manner and assist them in some situations

tasks.taskName: Shows interest in the behavior of others
tasks.taskObjective: The student will attend to or show an interest in the physical and verbal behavior of peers.
tasks.question: Does the student attend to or show an interest in the behavior of peers?
tasks.examples: watches other children playing with a certain toy or pretending to be a popular children's character
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= attends to the physical and verbal behavior of peers, 1= attends to the physical actions of peers

tasks.taskName: Looks at others to start a social interaction
tasks.taskObjective: The student will look at others (peers and adults) in such a manner as to initiate a social interaction.
tasks.question: Does the student look at others in such a manner as to initiate a social interaction with both peers and adults?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= student regularly initiates social interactions with both peers and adults by looking at them, 1= student occasionally initiates social interaction by looking at an individual

tasks.taskObjective: The student will approach and attempt to physically engage others in interactions even when the other person does not have a reinforcing item.
tasks.question: Does the student approach and attempt to physically engage others in interactions even when the other person does not have a reinforcing item?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= frequently approaches and makes attempts to physically engage others in interactions, 1= occasionally approaches and makes attempts to physically engage others in interactions

tasks.taskName: Looks at others in anticipation of completing a reinforcing action
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to look at a person (in anticipation) just before the person is to complete an action that will produce a desired outcome?
tasks.question: Does the student look at the person who is about to do something to produce a desired outcome (e.g., about to release the end of a balloon to let it fly around the room)?
tasks.examples: Jack in the Box to pop open when you turn the handle, waits for you to release air from a balloon and let it fly around the room
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= usually looks at a person in anticipation of a repeat of a reinforcing action, 1= when provided with some additional verbal prompting, student looks at a person in anticipation of a repeat of a reinforcing action

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to follow simple known directions provided by another individual.
tasks.question: Does the student follow simple known directions?
tasks.examples: come here, turn around, sit down, stand up
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= follows known instructions from adults & peers at least 75% of the time, 1= usually follows known instructions from adults at least 75% of the time

tasks.taskObjective: The student will attend to and imitate the physical and verbal behavior of peers.
tasks.question: Does the student attend to the behavior of peers?
tasks.examples: Makes arm and hand movements while singing or listening to a song
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= imitates multiple-step sequences of motor and verbal behaviors exhibited by peers, 1= imitates simple, single-step movements of peers

tasks.taskObjective: The student will return greetings from others.
tasks.question: Does the student return greetings to others?
tasks.examples: Example of an indirect prompt = "What do you say?"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2=student returns greetings from peers without prompts, 1= student returns greetings from peers but often requires an indirect verbal prompt

tasks.taskName: Physically prompts others to do activities
tasks.taskObjective: The student will approach and attempt to physically prompt others to do a specific activity.
tasks.question: Does the student approach and attempt to physically prompt others to do a specific activity?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= often makes independent multiple attempts, 3= sometimes makes independent multiple attempts, 2= makes single independent attempts, 1= makes a single attempt when prompted

tasks.taskName: Responds to approaches & attempts to interact from peers
tasks.taskObjective: The student will respond appropriately to the attempts of peers to engage the student in an interaction (e.g., play with a toy or game, participate in an outdoor activity).
tasks.question: Does the student go along with the attempts of peers to engage the student in an interaction (e.g., play with a toy or game, participate in an outdoor activity)?
tasks.examples: Peer asks student to join a game of "Duck, Duck, Goose" and the student sits down with the other students
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily goes along with interactions initiated by peers in most positive situations, 1= when carefully approached, goes along with interactions initiated by some peers, in some situations

tasks.taskName: Sharing: gives- up items to others
tasks.taskObjective: The student will allow others to use items which he is using/ possesses.
tasks.question: Does the student allow others to use items which he is using/ possesses?
tasks.examples: Allows others to take items
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= usually without prompts 1= does when prompted

tasks.taskObjective: The student will try to locate a significant person when that person leaves the child's visual field.
tasks.question: Does the child try to locate a significant person when that person leaves the child's visual field?
tasks.examples: A peer is playing with the student but goes into a different section of the room and the student tries to find his peer.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= will usually seek a missing person when he has been engaged in a fun activity with the peer or adult, 1= will seek the missing person when the person leaves with a reinforcing item

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to initiate an interaction with others and then look to see who is watching him before engaging in an action.
tasks.question: Does the student engage in actions to get attention from others and then look to see that others are attending to him?
tasks.examples: Student climbs to the top of the slide, stomps his feet on the top, says "Here I go" and then looks to ensure others are watching him before he goes down the slide
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= engage in actions to get others to attend to what he is about to do and ensure they are attending to him at least 3 times per day, 1= engage in actions to get others to attend to what he is about to do and ensure they are attending to him at least 6 times per week (Note: these actions do not include "disruptive behavior" that result in attention from others)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously label items for both adults and peers.
tasks.question: Does the student spontaneously label items for both adults and peers?
tasks.examples: Student sees an airplane in the sky and points toward it and says "airplane"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= Labels multiple items for 3 peers and adults without prompts, 3= single label for 1 peer & multiple for adults without prompts, 2= single label for 1 peer without prompts, 1= single label for adults without prompts

tasks.taskObjective: The student will make appropriate eye contact when interacting with others.
tasks.question: Does the student make and maintain appropriate eye contact while interacting with others?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= when as a listener & speaker with adults & peers, 1= when as a listener & speaker with adults

tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask peers for (single) items.
tasks.question: Does the student ask peers for an item?
tasks.examples: Asks a peer for a toy car
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= Spontaneously and frequently asks peers for items without prompts, 1= asks peers for items with prompts

tasks.taskName: Sharing: asks for items to be shared
tasks.taskObjective: The student will ask others to share their items (multiple) with him.
tasks.question: Does the student ask others to share some of their items?
tasks.examples: Play with toys together, each have a portion of items available
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= usually without prompts 1= does when prompted

tasks.taskObjective: The student will offer to share items with others.
tasks.question: Does the student offer to share items with others?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= often makes independent multiple attempts, 3= sometimes makes independent multiple attempts, 2= makes single independent attempts, 1= makes a single attempt when prompted

tasks.taskObjective: The student will appropriately initiate greetings to others.
tasks.question: Does the student initiate greetings to others?
tasks.examples: Example of an indirect prompt = "Look who is here"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2=student greets peers without prompts, 1= student greets peers but often requires a verbal prompt

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to approach peers and join an ongoing activity.
tasks.question: Does the student approach and join peers who are engaging in an activity?
tasks.examples: Children are playing a game of "tag" and the child joins the activity, children are making a building with blocks and the student goes to the group and helps
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= without it being suggested by an adult, student will join a group of peers engaged in a desired ongoing activity, 1= when suggested by an adult, student will join a group of peers engaged in a desired ongoing activity

tasks.taskName: Observation of peers’ attention to activities
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to attend to peers’ orientation to items and events.
tasks.question: Does the student notice and shift his attention when his peers shift their attention to an interesting item or activity?
tasks.examples: Children notice a teacher opens a bottle of bubbles and run to the teacher... The student notices the children leaving and goes to see what is happening
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= will usually look at or approach and investigate an item or activity when a few peers turn to look at or show an interest in an item or event, 1= will usually approach and investigate an item or activity when a large group of his peers points to an item or changes location and shows an interest in a particular item or event

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to follow directions from peers to adjust his behavior to be more socially acceptable.
tasks.question: Does the student allow peers to give him instructions regarding socially acceptable behavior?
tasks.examples: stand an appropriate distance from others, sit quietly, talk in a quiet voice, remain in line, keep hands to self
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= usually follows both stated and implied directions from peers in a variety of contexts, 1= follows stated directions from at least one peer to adjust his behavior in at least one situation

tasks.taskName: Adjusts behavior based on changes in peer's actions
tasks.taskObjective: During a task-related activity, the student will be able to observe changes in a peer's behavior and adjust his actions to correspond to the peer.
tasks.question: During a task-related activity, does the student observe changes in a peer's actions and make adjustments to his own actions?
tasks.examples: Stops walking when peers stop (without holding hands), carry a box with a peer without spilling contents
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= usually attends to and makes adjustments based on a peer's actions, 1= occasionally attends to and makes adjustments to task related activity based on a peer's actions

tasks.taskObjective: When others indicate that they are unable to get to something or unable to see or hear something, the student will arrange the materials so the peer can participate in the activity.
tasks.question: Does the student notice that a peer needs help to see, hear, or do something and then helps adjust the situation so the peer can enjoy the activity?
tasks.examples: A peer cannot see a picture in a book so the student moves to the side to let the peer be able to see the book.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= will usually make adjustments to accommodate a peer when the peer indirectly indicates a problem (I can't see it"), 1= will usually make adjustments to accommodate a peer when the peer asked the student to take a certain action (e.g., "move over")

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to state items and activities that are enjoyed by others and state which people like a particular item or activity.
tasks.question: Does the student know the likes and dislikes of others?
tasks.examples: States that Jake likes bananas but Emily does not like them. When asked who might want part of a banana he says "Jake"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= knows at least 2 specific things enjoyed or not enjoyed by at least 4 people, 1=knows at least 2 specific things enjoyed or not enjoyed by at least 2 people

tasks.taskName: Direct others attention to something of interest to them
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to know what activities, news or items would be of interest to specific individuals and will direct their attention to those items.
tasks.question: Does the student direct others to see things that they know would be of interest to that particular individual?
tasks.examples: Student knows that Jason likes soccer, so he tells Jason that Tyler brought a soccer ball to school today
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= frequently directs several different peers and adults to items and activities that would be of interest to each person, 1= can direct at least one individual to something that is of interest to that person at least twice per week

tasks.taskName: Attends to the reactions of interest by others
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to attend to and respond to feedback from others that indicate their interest in a topic or activity.
tasks.question: Does the student notice if others are enjoying an activity or conversation and change what they are doing based on those observations?
tasks.examples: Student talks about their favorite movie character but notices that a peer isn't interested so he seeks a different peer who is interested in the topic
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= will usually notice from a peer's facial feedback (e.g., smiles and looks interested, looks away) that he is interested or not interested in something, 1= will respond to peer's level of interest only when directly told by the peer that they are or are not interested

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to go to a person repeat a short message that he was asked to say to the person.
tasks.question: Is the student able to deliver a short message to others?
tasks.examples: Mom asks child to "ask Daddy to come help me "and child walks into another room and says "Mommy wants help"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can find a specified person, get their attention and deliver a four-word message after going into an adjoining room to deliver the message, 1= can deliver a three-word message after going across a room to deliver the message

tasks.taskName: Waits for break in conversation to interrupt
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to wait for a break in an on-going conversation before attempting to speak with one of the people involved in the conversation.
tasks.question: Does the student wait for the appropriate time to enter a conversation? Does he wait to speak if given a hand signal to wait until there is further acknowledgement from one of the speakers?
tasks.examples: Two people are talking and the child waits for acknowledgement (look at him) from one of the people before he begins to talk
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= when others are talking, usually waits for a person to look at him before speaking or appropriately attempts to catch speakers' attention ("excuse me"), 1= will wait for speakers to finish if given a hand signal to wait by one of the speakers

tasks.taskObjective: The student will converse with adults and peers for up to three exchanges.
tasks.question: Does the student converse with others?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= at least 3 exchanges with adults & peers, 3= 2 exchanges with adults & peers, 2= 1 exchange with adults & peers, 1= 1 exchange with adults

tasks.taskObjective: The student will spontaneously ask both peers and adults for information.
tasks.question: Does the student spontaneously ask both peers and adults for information?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= frequently and spontaneously asks peers and adults for information 1= occasionally will spontaneously ask an individual for information

tasks.taskName: Obtains and maintains attention of others
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to get and maintain another individual's attention prior to presenting an instruction to that individual.
tasks.question: Does the student get others' attention while attempting to interact even when the other person may not initially respond to the child's attempt to get a person's attention?
tasks.examples: Calls a person's name, taps person on shoulder, physically moves into a person's line of sight
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= successfully obtains and maintains interaction with peers & adults, 3= will persist in attempting to get attention from adults and peers, 2= can get attention from responsive adults & peers, 1= can get attention from responsive adults

tasks.taskObjective: The student will sit without engaging in disruptive behavior during small group instruction.
tasks.question: Does the student sitin a small group teaching situation without disrupting others (e.g., attempting to leave the group, touching other children, distracting repetitive behavior, making non-task-related noises)?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 1:4 group for 15 min., 3= 1:3 group for 10 min., 2= 1:2 group for 10 min., 1= 1:2 group for 5 min.

tasks.taskObjective: The student will sit without engaging in disruptive behavior during group instruction.
tasks.question: Does the student sitin a group teaching situation without disrupting others (e.g., attempting to leave the group, touching other children, distracting repetitive behavior, making non-task-related noises)?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 1:16 group for 15 min., 3= 1:12 (OR 2:16) for 15 min., 2= 1:8 for 15 min., 1= 1:6 for 15 minutes

tasks.taskObjective: The student will attend to a teacher during small group instruction.
tasks.question: Does the student attend to the teacher in a group teaching situation?
tasks.examples: Student orients towards and follows directions given by the teacher
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 1:4 group for 75% of time, 3= 1:3 group 75%, 2= 1:2 group for 75%, 1= 1:2 group for 50% of time

tasks.taskName: Attends to other students in group
tasks.taskObjective: The student will attend to the responses given by other students during small group instruction.
tasks.question: Does the student attend to the responses given by other students in a group teaching situation?
tasks.examples: Student orients towards other students who are talking and watches or listens to the other students' responses
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 1:4 group for 75% of time, 3= 1:3 group 75%, 2= 1:2 group for 75%, 1= 1:2 group for 50% of time

tasks.taskName: Follows group instructions- all do the same receptive response
tasks.taskObjective: The student will follow instructions presented to a group of students.
tasks.question: Does the student follow instructions which are given to a group of students?
tasks.examples: Everybody put your hands on your head.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=In a 1:4 group responds at the same time as others respond for 75% of known instructions, 3= 1:3 group 75%, 2= 1:2 group for 75%, 1= 1:2 group for 50% of known instructions

tasks.taskName: Follows group instructions with a discrimination
tasks.taskObjective: The student will follow instructions presented to a group of students which require the student to make a discrimination.
tasks.question: Does the student follow instructions which are given to a group of students which require the student to make a discrimination?
tasks.examples: If you have a green shin, stand up, --- if wearing a red shirt, line up
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4=In a 1:4 group responds at the same time as others respond for 75% of known instructions, 3= 1:3 group 75%, 2= 1:2 group for 75%, 1= 1:2 group for 50% of known instructions

tasks.taskName: Raises hand to get teacher attention to do an activity
tasks.taskObjective: The student will raise his hand to respond to questions presented to the group of students regarding who would like to do an activity.
tasks.question: Does the student raise his/her hand when the teacher asks a group of students who would like to be selected to do an activity?
tasks.examples: When the teacher asks "Who would like to pick the next song?" the student raises his hand to be called on to answer the question
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= independently raises hand to request to be selected to do a preferred activity on at least 50% of opportunities presented to a group of at least 8 students, 1= independently raises hand to request to be selected to do a preferred activity on at least 50% of opportunities presented to a group of at least 4 students

tasks.taskName: Raises hand to answer a question
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to raise his hand to answer simple questions.
tasks.question: Can the student raise his hand to answer a question?
tasks.examples: Raise your hand if you came to school on a bus, raise your hand if you want a chocolate chip cookie ---basically a yes/no response
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can independently respond to questions, 1= requires only a gestural prompt for less than 50 % of known questions.

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to raise his hand and name an item being displayed.
tasks.question: Can the student raise his hand to be called upon and then name an item being displayed?
tasks.examples: Group question - Teacher asks "Who knows what this is?" the student raises his hand and gives answer when called on by teacher
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can independently raise hand and name known items, 1= requires only a gestural prompt for less than 50 % of known items to raise hand and name the item

tasks.taskName: Raises hand AND answers a question
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to raise his hand to answer simple questions about items that are not present.
tasks.question: Can the student raise his hand to answer a question about items that are not present?
tasks.examples: Group question - Everybody, who knows...What can we eat for breakfast?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can independently raise hand and answer known questions about items that are not present, 1= requires only a gestural prompt for less than 50 % of known questions to raise hand and answer question

tasks.taskObjective: The student will appropriately take turns with other students during group instruction activities.
tasks.question: Does the student take turns during group instruction?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= takes turns appropriately & 75% time without prompts, 1= 75% with prompts

tasks.taskName: Learns new skills in group teaching format
tasks.taskObjective: The student will readily acquire new academic skills during group instruction activities.
tasks.question: Does the student learn new academic skills while participating in group instruction?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily acquires new skills, 1= acquires some skills with repetitive exposure to the material

tasks.taskObjective: The student will independently follow daily classroom routines.
tasks.question: Does the student follow classroom activities such as putting away his lunch, hang-up coat, etc.?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= independently, 1= 50% without verbal prompts

tasks.taskName: Works independently on non- academic activities
tasks.taskObjective: The student will work independently on non- educational or leisure-type activities.
tasks.question: Will the student remain on-task when instructed to independently engage in non-academic activities?
tasks.examples: Puzzles
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 minutes, 3= 15 minutes, 2= 10 minutes, 1=5 minutes

tasks.taskName: Sits and waits appropriately during transitions
tasks.taskObjective: When seated during classroom transitions the student will wait appropriately for the next activity to begin.
tasks.question: Does the student sit and wait appropriately during transitions from one known activity to the next?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= independently for up to 2 minutes, 1= independently for up to 30 seconds

tasks.taskName: Physically transitions to next area or activity
tasks.taskObjective: The student will make appropriate transitions while following directions to move from one area to another in the classroom to change educational activities.
tasks.question: Does the student successfully transition from one known activity to the next?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= independently, 1= 50% without prompts

tasks.taskName: Waits turn to do activities (wash hands, etc.)
tasks.taskObjective: The student will wait appropriately for his turn during classroom activities.
tasks.question: Does the student wait appropriately until his turn to do an activity (e.g., wait in line to wash hands or go outside for recess)?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= independently for up to 2 minutes, 1= independently for up to 30 seconds

tasks.taskObjective: The student will follow instructions to form a line and wait appropriately while standing in the line.
tasks.question: Does the student line-up upon request?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= independently, 1= 50% of instructions without prompts

tasks.taskObjective: The student will work independently on known educational activities.
tasks.question: Will the student remain on-task when instructed to independently engage in academic activities?
tasks.examples: Worksheets
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= 20 minutes, 3= 15 minutes, 2= 10 minutes, 1= 5 minutes

tasks.taskObjective: The student will follow instructions to get and return his own educational materials.
tasks.question: Can the student get and put away his own educational activities?
tasks.examples: Student puts his workbook into his storage area when told to do so at the end of a task
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= independently, 1= 50% of instructions without prompts

tasks.taskName: Completes a task and brings work to teacher or puts away materials
tasks.taskObjective: The student will follow instructions to complete a task and bring the work to the teacher or return his own educational materials.
tasks.question: Can the student follow instructions to complete a task and bring the work to the teacher or return his own educational materials?
tasks.examples: Without being reminded at the end of the task, the student puts his workbook into his storage area when an assigned task is finished
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= independently, 1= 50% of instructions without prompts

tasks.taskName: Stands and waits appropriately during transitions
tasks.taskObjective: During classroom transitions the student will stand and wait appropriately for the next activity to begin.
tasks.question: Does the student stand and wait appropriately during transitions from one known activity to the next?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= independently for up to 3 minutes, 1= 50% without prompts

tasks.taskObjective: The student will use skills acquired with one item with similar examples of that item.
tasks.question: Does the student use skills acquired with one item to emit the same response with a similar example of that item?
tasks.examples: Student is taught to label a brown cup as "cup." Student now labels green, yellow and striped cups as "cup"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= acquires label & receptive responses with 1 stimulus & immediately generalizes to many stimuli within the class within 2 trials, 1= generalizes to similar items within 10 trials

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use skills learned with one instructor with other instructors.
tasks.question: Does the student use skills learned with one instructor with other instructors?
tasks.examples: Student learns to label "cup" with one instructor and can then label "cup" for other instructors
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily uses acquired skills with novel instructors, 1= works readily with 4 or more instructors

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use skills acquired in training situations in other situations.
tasks.question: Does the student use skills acquired in training situations in other situations?
tasks.examples: Student learns to label "cup" at school and can then label "cup" at home
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= readily uses acquired skills without prompts outside of the original training situation, 1= uses acquired skills outside of the original training situation with minimal verbal prompts

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use skills acquired in individual teaching sessions when in group situations with peers.
tasks.question: Does the student use skills acquired in individual teaching sessions when in group situations with peers?
tasks.examples: Student learns to label "cup" in an individualized teaching session and can then label "cup" while participating in a small group discussion
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously uses acquired skills under group situations, 1= uses skills in groups only with minimal verbal prompts

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use other appropriate responses after learning a response to a given situation.
tasks.question: After learning an appropriate response to a given situation, does the student use other alternative appropriate responses under those same conditions?
tasks.examples: Upon seeing a dog, the student may say "dog, "puppy," "K-9," "pooch," etc. When answering question regarding "things to eat, " the student may say "apple, banana, bread," OR "cake, pizza, apple"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= spontaneously uses a variety of appropriate responses rather than a single response and uses variation in responses with multiple components, 1= uses some alternative responses with minimal verbal prompts

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to use words acquired during one type of language skill to other types of language skills.
tasks.question: Can the student learn words during one type of language skill training then use the acquired word in other types of language skills?
tasks.examples: When taught "cup" as a label, the child then can ask for "cup" and can receptively identify cups. When student is taught to receptively identify a cup when told "you drink from it", the student is able to say "cup" when asked "What do you drink from?"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= When student is taught to receptively identify an item when given its function, the student can then state the item when verbally told its function, 1= When taught the name of an item, the child then can ask for and receptively identify the item

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to receptively identify upper and lower case letters.
tasks.question: Can the student receptively identify upper and lower case letters?
tasks.examples: When shown three letters, the student can point to the letter "B" upon request
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can identify all 26 upper & lower case letters, 3= can identify a total of at least 15 upper or lower case letters, 2= can identify at least a total of 10 upper or lower case letters, 1= can identify at least a total of 5 upper or lower case letters

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to name upper and lower case letters.
tasks.question: Can the student name upper and lower case letters?
tasks.examples: When shown the printed letter "B" and asked "What letter is this?" the student says "B"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can label all 26 upper & lower case letters, 3= can label a total of at least 15 upper or lower case letters, 2= can label at least a total of 10 upper or lower case letters, 1= can label at least a total of 5 upper or lower case letters

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to select the corresponding letter when given the sounds associated with letter.
tasks.question: Can the student select the corresponding letter when given the sounds associated with letter?
tasks.examples: "Give me the one that makes the sound "ssss"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can identify the sounds of at least 20 letters, 3= can identify the sounds of at least 10 letters, 2= can identify the sounds of at least 5 letters, 1= can identify the sounds of at least 2 letters

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to give the sounds associated with letters.
tasks.question: Can the student give the sounds associated with letters?
tasks.examples: "What sound does this letter make?" while showing the student the letter 'b'
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can identify the sounds of at least 20 letters, 3= can identify the sounds of at least 10 letters, 2= can identify the sounds of at least 5 letters, 1= can identify the sounds of at least 2 letters

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to match words to pictures.
tasks.question: Can the student match words to pictures?
tasks.examples: When given a card with the written word "bat', and an array of three pictures on the table (bat, cat, and hat), the student will put the written word with the matching picture (bat).
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can match at least 20 words with corresponding pictures, 3= can match at least 10 words with corresponding pictures, 2= can match at least 5 words with corresponding pictures, 1= can match at least 2 words with corresponding pictures

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to match word cards to those same words written in different fonts presented in a display of three word cards.
tasks.question: Can the student match word cards to the same words written in different fonts when words are presented in a display of three word cards?
tasks.examples: When given a card with the written word "bat', and an array of three cards on the table (bat, cat, and hat), the student will put the card with the matching word card (bat).
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= different fonts with only 1 letter different in non-target words 3= same fonts 1 letter different, 2= same fonts 2 letters different in non-matching words, 1= same fonts with 3 or more different letters in non-matching words

tasks.taskName: Names letters in words reading left to right
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to name the letters of words reading from left to right across the word.
tasks.question: Can the student name the letters of words reading from left to right across the word?
tasks.examples: When presented with the word 'hat' the student will say "h," "a," "
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can point to and name the letters of 5 letter words (left to right) without prompts, 1= can point to and name the letters of 3 letter words (left to right) with only one prompt per word

tasks.taskName: Match individual letters to letters on word card
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to match individual letters to the letters on cards with single 5 letter words.
tasks.question: Can the student match individual letters to the letters on cards with single 5 letter words?
tasks.examples: Given a word card with the word "train," the student will match individual letter cards to the letters on the word card
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can match letters for words up to 5 letters in length when given extra letters, some of which are similar (e.g., e & a), 1= can match letters for words up to 3 letters in length when not given extra letters, and the letters are not similar (e.g., bat)

tasks.taskName: Fill in missing letter of words
tasks.taskObjective: Given a picture of an object and two of three letters provided, the student will be able to add a small letter card to complete three letter words.
tasks.question: Can the student add a small letter card to complete three letter words when given a picture of an object and two of three letters for the word provided?
tasks.examples: Given a picture of a cat and the written display c__t, the student will add the "a" to complete the word
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can add a letter in any position of the word for at least 10 words, 1= can add a letter at least one position of the word for at least 5 words

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to read words.
tasks.question: Can the student read words?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can read at least 50 words, 3= can read at least 20 words, 2= can read at least 10 words, 1= can read at least 5 words

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to decode unknown words.
tasks.question: Can the student decode/sound-out unknown words?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can sound-out 20 words of 4 or more letters including words that the student doesn't know receptively or as a label, 1= can sound out any consonant-vowel- consonant words using known phonemes

tasks.taskName: Read small groups of words from left to right
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to read phrases.
tasks.question: Can the student read phrases?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can read any phrase containing combinations of known words, 3= can read 10 three word phrases, 2= can read 5 three word phrases, 1= can read 2 three word phrases

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to read sentences.
tasks.question: Can the student read sentences?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can read any sentence containing combinations of known words, 3= can read 10 four to six word sentences, 2= can read 5 four to six word sentences, 1= can read 2 four to six word sentences

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to choose a word from a selection of words to fill in a missing word when given an incomplete sentence.
tasks.question: Can the student choose a word from a selection of words to fill in a missing word when given an incomplete sentence?
tasks.examples: Score 1=The ____has fur. (cat frog) Score 2= The wore hats. (pen men pet)
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can select the appropriate word from an array of 3 words which differ on less than 50% of the letters, 1= can select the appropriate word from an array of 2 words which differ on more than 50% of the letters

tasks.taskName: Reads and follows simple instructions to do actions
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to read and follow simple instructions to perform an action.
tasks.question: Can the student read and follow simple instructions to perform an action (e.g., Give the red cup to Mommy, Give Daddy a hug)?
tasks.examples: Go get a cup, Put the doll in the bed, Give the doll a hug, Put the cup in the sink, Give Jason a pencil, Put the shoe in the box, Put Dad's hat on your head.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can read at least 20 sentences and perform at least 6 different actions, 1= can read at least 10 sentences and perform at least 3 different actions (e.g., give, get, put on, put in)

tasks.taskName: Reads and follows simple instructions on worksheets
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to read and follow simple instructions on worksheets.
tasks.question: Can the student read and follow simple instructions on worksheets (e.g., put a circle around the bird, draw a line under the shoe)?
tasks.examples: Draw a line from the monkey to the banana, underline the letter 'A’, put an 'X" on the circle, color the square red, draw a box around the tree, write the number 3 in the triangle, etc.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can read at least 20 sentences and follow at least 6 different directions, 1= can read at least 10 sentences and follow at least 3 different directions (e.g., circle, underline, color)

tasks.taskName: Read passages and answer comprehension questions
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to read sentences and answer questions regarding the sentence.
tasks.question: Can the student read sentences and answer questions regarding the sentence?
tasks.examples: Student reads "The man was sitting on a brown horse" and then answers the question "Who was sitting on the horse?"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can read at least three sentences and answer simple questions regarding the content, 1= can read a single sentence and answer a simple question regarding the content

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to continue counting to 10 when the counting sequence is started for him.
tasks.question: Can the student continue counting to 10 when the sequence is started for him?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can continue counting to 10 if started with "1, 2", 1= can count along with instructor to 10 (vocal imitation)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to rote count to any specified number up to 30.
tasks.question: Can the student rote count to any specified number up to 307?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can count to any specified number up to 30, 3= can count to 30, 2= can count to 20, 1=can count to 10

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to continue counting objects to 10 when the counting sequence is started for him.
tasks.question: Can the student continue counting objects to 10 when the sequence is started for him?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can continue counting objects to 10 if started with "1, 2", 1=can count along with instructor to 10 (vocal imitation) even if the instructor varies the pace of the counting (e.g., 1, 2, ....(pause) 3,...4,5...6, etc)

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to count the number of items given to him even if the items are not arranged in a straight row.
tasks.question: Can the student count items given to him (with 1 to 1 correspondence) even if the items are not arranged in a straight row?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can count any amount up to 100, 3= can count any amount up to 20, 2= can count any amount up to 10, 1= can count any amount up to 5 even if the items are not presented in a row (i.e., slightly scattered)

tasks.taskName: Count out objects from a larger set
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to count-out a specified number of items from a larger set of items.
tasks.question: Can the student count- out a specified number of items from a larger set of items?
tasks.examples: When the student is given 7 blocks and asked to "Give me 5 blocks" the student will count out 5 blocks
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can count any amount up to 30, 3= can count any amount up to 20, 2= can count any amount up to 10, 1=can count any amountup to 5

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to name the numerals on a number line.
tasks.question: Can the student name the numerals on a number line?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= will name the numerals 1 to 10 on a number line, 1= will name the numerals on a number line when verbally prompted "1,2.." while instructor points to the numerals.

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to name numbers to 100.
tasks.question: Can the student name numbers?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can identify numbers to 100, 3= can identify numbers to 30, 2= can identify numbers to 20, 1= can identify numbers to 10

tasks.taskName: Match number with same amount of objects
tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to match numbers with the same amount of items and vice versa.
tasks.question: Can the student match numbers with the same amount of items and vice versa?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 4= can match items with numbers to 30 (and vice versa), 3= can match items with numbers to 20, 2= can match items with numbers to 10, 1= can match items with numbers to 5

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to receptively identify and label examples of the word "more".
tasks.question: Can the student receptively identify and label examples of the word "more"?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can both receptively identify and label, 1= can either receptively identify or label

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to receptively identify and label examples of the word "less".
tasks.question: Can the student receptively identify and label examples of the word "less"?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can both receptively identify and label, 1= can either receptively identify or label

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to receptively identify and label examples of the word "some".
tasks.question: Can the student receptively identify and label examples of the word "some"?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can both receptively identify and label, 1= can either receptively identify or label

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to receptively identify and label examples of the word "all".
tasks.question: Can the student receptively identify and label examples of the word "all"?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can both receptively identify and label, 1= can either receptively identify or label

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to receptively identify and label examples of the word "zero/none".
tasks.question: Can the student receptively identify and label examples of the word "zero/none"?
tasks.examples: Receptive- When shown two bowls, one with popcorn and the other empty, and asked "Which one has none?" the student touches the empty bowl. Labels- When shown an empty cookie jar and asked "How many cookies are in the jar?" the student says "none"
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can both receptively identify and label, 1= can either receptively identify or label

tasks.taskObjective: Given a set of items, the student will be able to get the correct number of additional items to make a set of a specified quantity.
tasks.question: Can the student determine how many more items are needed to make a set of a larger quantity?
tasks.examples: Given 2 spoons and asked to have a total of 4 spoons, the student will get 2 additional spoons.
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= physically places additional items to make a total set of up to 10 items, 1= physically places additional items to make a total set of up to 5 items.

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to receptively identify and label examples of the word "same".
tasks.question: Can the student receptively identify and label examples of the word "same"?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can both receptively identify and label, 1= can either receptively identify or label

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to receptively identify and label examples of the word "different".
tasks.question: Can the student receptively identify and label examples of the word "different"?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can both receptively identify and label, 1= can either receptively identify or label

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to receptively identify and label examples of the word "greater".
tasks.question: Can the student receptively identify and label examples of the word "greater"?
tasks.scoringCriteria: 2= can both receptively identify and label, 1= can either receptively identify or label

tasks.taskObjective: The student will be able to receptively identify and label examples of the word "add".
tasks.question: Can the student receptively identify and label examples of the word "add"?
tasks.examples: Receptive- When given five blocks in a dish and given some additional blocks and asked to "add two more" the student places additional blocks in the dish. Labels- When shown putting more beans in a jar and asked "What am I doing?" the student says "adding beans"
